instructions:
skep is a substrate of documents, immutable content and first-class links. You reach one board through this adapter, under ONE SIGNED SESSION it opened for your principal with its key: every write you make is your account's for good.

Call session_info first: who you act as, your key, the board, whether you may write. Call search before you write: link to what exists with make_link, or transclude it with copy, never retype it.

Change a draft's text with replace_text (one change), edit_text (several, all or none) or move_lines (lines moved). A published document is never edited in place: stage(from_) mints a draft holding its words, and publication_open with doc, publication_count, then publication_confirm publish it as doc's next version; publication_open with mint publishes any draft of yours as a new document.

Every burst (insert, delete, copy, reinstate, rearrange) carries as_of: the as_of of your last read of its document, or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. A burst typed against an older state comes back held, cause moved: drop it with resolve, read the document again, and send it afresh at the new as_of.

The board's refusal is data, in the result; isError means the shell could not get the board's verdict, or a tool's own error its card names. A write answered unreachable (isError), or refused poisoned or internal_panic (data), may have landed: read before you send it again. A burst the shell keeps answers held: held lists your held lines, resolve acts on each.

help() lists the help topics; help("HELD BURSTS") reads one; help("replace_text") reads a tool's full reference. A capitalised name in parentheses, such as (HELD BURSTS), is a help topic: read it before you first use the tools that name it.

One naming note: in make_link, emit and stage, the schema argument from_ is the wire's from.
commons_instructions: The commons is at {addr}: link-type names are addresses in its subspace 3, each documented by a link of type {addr}.0.3.50 ("defines").

tools.name: create_new_document
tools.description: Mint a fresh empty document in account (your own account: resolve it via principal_prefix or session_info). Response: ack_addr with the document's address.

account.description: Account address the document is minted in.

tools.name: delegate
tools.description: Carve new_prefix off your account (or node) and register principal new_id as its owner, atomically. Obtain new_prefix from next_account_prefix; only the owner of the parent may delegate under it. Response: ack_addr with the minted account address.

new_prefix.description: The delegable prefix tumbler, as answered by next_account_prefix.

new_id.description: The principal id registered as the new account's owner.

tools.name: register_node
tools.description: Admit a provisioned node address (bootstrap provisioning; the address is supplied, not minted). Response: ack_addr.

addr.description: The provisioned node address (a raw tumbler).

tools.name: fork
tools.description: Mint a fresh EMPTY account-tier document in your own account. Shares no content: the content-sharing fork is version; the staging act, which copies and records where the draft began, is stage. Response: ack_addr.

tools.name: stage
tools.description: THE STAGING ACT, one operation: mint a fresh PRIVATE document in your own account holding from_'s whole content by identity, and record in the board's own state where the draft began — its base (the version member you stage a change to, or the document itself while it has no version yet), its source, and how much the copy took — in ONE commit; a refused frame leaves nothing, and there is no record for you to write. from_ (the wire's from — renamed in this schema only, mapped back by the adapter) is that member or memberless document, or another private draft of yours for an alternative of it, which inherits that draft's recorded base. Always private and never signed; an empty account mints its home first (mint_home_first); a source you may not read is withheld. Read the record back with doc_metadata(draft): base and base_copied, moved to the member each publication of the draft makes, and source. Response: ack_addr with the draft's address.

from_.description: The version member, memberless document or private draft of yours the new draft is copied from (the wire's from).

tools.name: create_well_known_document
tools.description: Create one of your account's four well-known documents, at <account>.0.<slot>. slot is REQUIRED: 2 your mailbox, always private; 3 your bio, 4 your public link page, 5 your policy document — each of 3 to 5 created PUBLISHED and EMPTY, its first version written as any is: stage from it, write in the draft, publish naming it as doc. account is your own. Safe to call again: a second call at a slot answers the same address with committed: false, nothing written. An account with no home page yet is refused mint_home_first: create_new_document first. On a claimed board slots 3 to 5 need a signed session (signed_session_required). Response: ack_addr with the document's address. Full reference: help("create_well_known_document").

account.description: Your own account's address: the account whose well-known document is created.

slot.description: The well-known slot, by its document number: 2 the mailbox (private), 3 the bio, 4 the link page, 5 the account's policy document (each published and empty). REQUIRED.

tools.name: next_account_prefix
tools.description: The next delegable prefix under parent (what delegate demands). Response: maybe_addr; addr null means an ineligible parent.

tools.name: principal_prefix
tools.description: Any principal's account address (public, immutable registry data). Response: maybe_addr; addr null means an unknown principal.

tools.name: effective_owner
tools.description: Who owns addr: the LONGEST registered prefix containing it and the principal seated there, from one walk of the board's principal list. addr is any address in the board's local form; it need not be allocated. Response: effective_owner — {prefix, principal}, both present together, or null together where no registered principal's prefix contains addr. An account is allocated iff prefix equals the address asked; any other prefix names the nearest seat ABOVE it. Public registry data: no session needed, nothing withheld.

addr.description: Any address in this board's local form.

tools.name: doc_metadata
tools.description: A document's publication record: doc (the trunk a version member projects to), published, owner, birth (its first version), source (what a version or a stage minted it sharing: a fork's parent, a staged draft's source), base (a staged draft's recorded base: the version its next publication lands after, moved to the member each publication of it makes; null for a draft never staged), merge (the marker of a merge landed in the draft), own_count (the content positions the address named holds itself, never its head's), and arranged_at (the position its text last changed at, its newest version's for a published document; an edit typed before it fails the typed-state check, arrangement_moved). Read a draft's base here, or ask publication_standing where it stands, before you publish it. Response: doc_metadata; refused withheld for a document you may not read, doc_not_registered for none. Full reference: help("doc_metadata").

doc.description: The document or version member asked about.

tools.name: key_set
tools.description: The credential table of account: who can sign for it, now and historically — enrolled and retired entries, each with its fingerprint and key. Principal-free: no session needed, a guest and a bound principal answered byte-identically. Response: key_set; a non-account address rejects not_an_account; a keyless account answers empty lists (such an account opens by reference, with a key enrolled in the nearest set above it).

tools.name: insert
tools.description: Insert content into doc at V-position at; each element of values is one write form. A bare string mints one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte (per-byte text, the substrate's text discipline); {"hex"} one per raw byte; {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} mint ONE composite value at one position whose interior is permanently unaddressable. Mixed arrays concatenate in order; an insert totalling zero values is refused empty_content. Response: ack_addr with the first minted I-address — or held, where the board does not take the burst or rejects it (HELD BURSTS): a held insert's address is never answered, so read the document once its line is gone.

at.description: Insertion V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

values.description: Write forms, concatenated in order. "" and {"hex": ""} are vacuous; a zero-byte atom is not expressible.

oneOf.description: Per-byte text: one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte.
Per-byte raw bytes: one single-byte value per byte.
ONE composite value of the string's UTF-8 bytes, at one position; its interior is permanently unaddressable.
ONE composite value of the raw bytes, at one position; interior permanently unaddressable.

deposit.description: The deposit declaration (PUB-2.59, PUB-2.64, PUB-9.13): the TYPE ADDRESS of the record class this insert's atom is of — the same type the make_link naming the atom then carries (PUB-2.63) — saying this insert is a deposit-class record atom landing at fresh positions past the document's arranged extent. A published document admits ONLY a deposit declared under a type its deposit class holds (today the enroll type 1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.1 and the retire type 1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.2), at fresh positions; an undeclared insert into it, one declared under any other type, or a declared one touching an arranged position, is refused published_target (stage the change in a draft, then publish it as the next version). Into a draft the declaration is inert. Absent means not a deposit; true, false and null are malformed.

as_of.description: The document state this insert was typed against (wire.md §Arrangement; the typed state): the as_of of your last read of doc — retrieve_v, image, retrieve_doc_v_span_set or line_numbers — or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. REQUIRED. The board refuses an insert typed against an older state of the document's arrangement arrangement_moved, carrying site.as_of (yours, echoed) and site.current (the position the document last changed at); read the document again and place your text against what it holds now.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Remove width positions of doc starting at p. Response: ack — or held (HELD BURSTS).

p.description: First removed V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("2"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

as_of.description: The document state this delete was typed against (wire.md §Arrangement; the typed state): the as_of of your last read of doc, or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. REQUIRED; typed against an older arrangement it is refused arrangement_moved with site.as_of and site.current.

tools.name: copy
tools.description: Transclude the given source spans into doc at at — shared identity, not copied bytes. Response: ack — or held (HELD BURSTS).

at.description: Destination V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

specs.description: V-specs naming the transcluded source spans.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} = subspace 1, ordinal 1, five positions; zero-width is invalid.

as_of.description: The DESTINATION doc's state this copy was typed against (wire.md §Arrangement; the typed state): the as_of of your last read of doc, or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. REQUIRED; typed against an older arrangement of doc it is refused arrangement_moved with site.as_of and site.current — the sources are not judged for it.

tools.name: reinstate
tools.description: Place runs of permanent content I-addresses into doc at at, by identity — shared identity, not copied bytes: the bytes a delete un-arranged come back at their own addresses, and every link on them returns. Each run is origin, i_start, width, as image answers a run of a document's words — i_start its first content I-address; every address must hold a value, and each origin must be a document you may read. A published doc refuses it published_target, which holds it (HELD BURSTS). Response: ack — or held.

doc.description: Destination document address (a draft you own).

at.description: Destination V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

runs.description: The I-runs to place, in order: each the document whose I-space it names, its first content I-address, and its width. Obtain a span's runs from image before removing it.

items.description: One run of permanent content I-addresses.

origin.description: The document the run's addresses were minted under (or a member of its chain).

i_start.description: The run's first content I-address, a full element position (doc.0.1.ordinal).

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("5"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

as_of.description: The DESTINATION doc's state this reinstate was typed against (wire.md §Arrangement; the typed state): the as_of of your last read of doc, or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. REQUIRED; typed against an older arrangement of doc it is refused arrangement_moved with site.as_of and site.current — the origins are not judged for it.

tools.name: rearrange
tools.description: Moves doc's content without copying it, so every unit keeps its identity and the links on it. cuts are content positions, strictly ascending, from 1 to one past the end; each stretch runs from its cut up to the next cut, not including it. THREE cuts a < b < c swap the two neighbouring stretches, so from a the content reads [b, c) then [a, b): cuts 2, 4, 6 over "abcde" give "adebc". FOUR cuts a < b < c < d swap the outer stretches [a, b) and [c, d) around the middle [b, c), which stays between them, so from a it reads [c, d), [b, c), [a, b): cuts 1, 2, 3, 4 over "abcde" give "cbade". The content outside is untouched. as_of as every burst carries it (THE TYPED STATE). The board's refusal comes back held, its cause the token — bad_cut_count, not_ascending, not_content_subspace, out_of_bounds, published_target — or moved for a stale burst: resolve(held, "drop"), then send it afresh, its cuts corrected against a fresh read. Response: ack — or held (HELD BURSTS).

cuts.description: Three or four cut V-positions, strictly ascending, all in the content subspace.

items.description: V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

as_of.description: The document state these cuts were typed against (wire.md §Arrangement; the typed state): the as_of of your last read of doc, or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. REQUIRED; typed against an older arrangement it is refused arrangement_moved with site.as_of and site.current, ahead of the cut count's own check.

tools.name: set_arrangement
tools.description: Set a draft's WHOLE content arrangement by identity in ONE commit: everything doc arranges is removed and the runs sent are placed from its start — shared identity, not copied bytes — so the draft holds what you sent or what it held. Use it to change a draft's whole text at once: one change of text is replace_text's, and merge_compose lands a merge for you. head and base record a merge: head the version it was composed on, base the base to record, merge its sides. Response: ack with at, your next as_of, and head_moved, the trunk's head, where a newer version than head stands. Refused fork_base_moved for a fork whose source is not head (fork afresh from the head), published_target for a published doc, no_base_to_record for a base on a draft with none. Never held: under halted writes it is refused at once. Full reference: help("set_arrangement").

doc.description: The draft whose whole arrangement is set (a draft you own).

runs.description: The whole arrangement, in order: each the document whose I-space it names, its first content I-address, and its width. May be empty, which empties the draft. Obtain runs from image.

items.description: One run of permanent content I-addresses.

origin.description: The document the run's addresses were minted under (or a member of its chain).

i_start.description: The run's first content I-address, a full element position (doc.0.1.ordinal).

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("5"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

as_of.description: The draft's state this arrangement was composed against (wire.md §Arrangement; the typed state): the as_of of your last read of doc, or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later. REQUIRED; composed against an older arrangement of doc it is refused arrangement_moved with site.as_of and site.current, and NOTHING is changed — the one refusal that keeps a landing from wiping an edit made since.

head.description: The version the merge was composed on, at the content count read of it (as doc_metadata's base_extent counts). Present on a merge's landing; absent on an undo and a plain re-arrangement. Checked against the draft's chain — a registered member of it (source_not_registered, then base_not_in_chain) — and the member's current count (base_extent_too_large), never against the current head: a newer head is told in the ack's head_moved. A draft with no recorded base and no published source checks its registration alone (source_not_registered), never its extent.

at.description: The head's address: a version member, or the document itself while it has no version.

extent.description: The head's content count as read when the merge was composed, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically.

base.description: The base to record for the draft, with the extent read of it: the head pair on a landing, the base read at the position before the landing on an undo. The draft's recorded base moves there in the same commit; absent, nothing of the record moves. A draft the board records no base for refuses it no_base_to_record; a base no mint has made source_not_registered; one off the draft's chain base_not_in_chain; an extent past the member's current count base_extent_too_large, as the head's is.

at.description: The member or memberless document to record as the base.

extent.description: The content count of it to record, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically.

merge.description: The merge the draft is to carry: its sides, by address, possibly empty, and at to put a taken-out merge back. Present only beside head, which is the marker's own; recorded only where base is recorded, as the marker travels with the base. Absent beside a base, the marker is cleared — the undo's shape.

sides.description: The sides merged, by address; empty where the draft itself was the side.

at.description: The position of the marker to put back — the at doc_metadata served for it before the merge was taken out. Absent for a landing, which the board stamps at its own commit. Requires base; a position naming no marker the board put on the draft since its last publication is refused marker_not_restorable, nothing written.

tools.name: make_link
tools.description: Create an open link homed in home. from_ is the wire's from, renamed in this schema alone. Each of from_, to and ty takes one form: a V-spec array, resolved against current arrangements and recorded as permanent I-spans; {"addrs": [addresses]}, the names recorded verbatim, one unit span each, nothing read — a link, a document, or a position nothing occupies; or {"spans": [{"start", "width"}]}, content I-spans recorded verbatim. ty must not be empty as given: an empty list, or a V-spec set resolving to nothing, is refused empty_type_resolution; from_ and to may be empty. replaces names the record whose state this link replaces, a second link typed replaces deposited beside it. Response: ack_addr with the link's address. Full reference: help("make_link").

tools.name: boards
tools.description: The shell's boards call: the one board this adapter serves, [{board, name, origin}] — board the shell's opaque reference, which no tool here takes (the adapter supplies it to the call that takes one), name and origin the board's origin.

tools.name: health
tools.description: The shell's health call for the board: {health, mode} — the board's GET /health answer verbatim, a live reading with no address ({ok, log_position, head_time, chain_head, auth: {claimant, local_trust, origins, signed_origins}, media, writes: {halted}}) and the mode derived from it: UNCLAIMED, CLAIMED-PERMISSIVE or ENFORCING. writes.halted true means the board takes no write until it restarts: a burst is held and sent by the shell once the board takes writes again (HELD BURSTS), and any other write is refused poisoned, as data.

tools.name: probe
tools.description: The shell's probe call: {daemon, reason?, dialed, signed} — the board's state, the most severe that holds: stopped where the shell runs the node, which this adapter never does; unreachable where the board does not answer; halted where its writes are halted until it restarts (health's writes.halted: a burst is held and sent by the shell once the board takes writes again, HELD BURSTS); head_unreadable where its head record will not read, reason saying why (no signed write can be made until it reads, and a burst is held head_unreadable); else running — the origin it is dialed at and the origin it is signed for.

tools.name: search
tools.description: The shell's search over the board's index at your reader class: query is words, matched across the published documents and the drafts you may read. Response: {hits, places, state, total, truncated, more_terms, fuzzy_bounded, positions_bounded} — each hit {doc, member, as_of, span: {start, width}, score, snippet: {text, start, marks}, kind: edition|draft (an edition is a published document), standing, occurrences, matched}; places the exact address or label matches; state the index's state ({arm: none|building|widening|complete|at_the_floor|resumed_from_the_floor|unplaced|past_the_ceiling|newer_skep|busy, ...}) — while it is none, building or busy a miss is not absence. A query past 1024 bytes is refused query_too_long.

query.description: The words to find; at most 1024 bytes.

opts.description: The search's options; each absent takes its default.

limit.description: At most this many hits (the index's own bound by default).

offset.description: Skip this many hits first (0 by default).

tools.name: places
tools.description: The shell's document listing: every document of the board's index you may read, in address order, each {doc, kind: edition|draft (an edition is a published document), label (its first line, or null), standing}, with the count per account and the index's state. opts.under narrows the listing to one address prefix (an account, a document). Response: {docs, counts: [{account, documents}], state} — while state.arm is none, building or busy the listing is not yet whole.

under.description: List the documents at or under this address prefix alone.

tools.name: held
tools.description: The shell's held call: your held bursts at the board, in resend order (HELD BURSTS). Each line names held, the ordinal resolve takes; doc; frame, the write as composed; and cause, why it is held: unreachable, halted, poisoned, durability, behind, head_unreadable or session_died, which the shell sends on its own once the board takes them; a refused run's token, or moved for a burst typed against an older state, each waiting on your resolve; or answers_lost, handed back to you. sent true means the write may have landed: read the document before you write it again. refusal is the verdict behind a refused or moved line; unwritable means the line stands in memory alone until the shell writes it to disk. Empty once every held burst has landed or been dropped: after a held answer, call it until the line is gone, then read what it wrote. Full reference: help("held").

tools.name: resolve
tools.description: The shell's resolve call: your act on a held line, by the ordinal held lists it under (HELD BURSTS). "drop" gives the line up for good, with the lines behind it on its document, in any state. "send" hands a refused run, a moved document's line or a line handed back (answers_lost) to the resend; on a line still holding it is not_resolvable, the shell sending it itself. A drop of a line with sent true reads first: {"kept": true} means its write landed, so nothing was dropped; refused landing_unread, the read could not tell — drop it again once the board answers. {"may_have_landed": [<ordinal>, …]} names lines dropped whose words may stand: read the document before you write them again. {} is done. Either act on a line the shell is sending at that moment is not_resolvable until that send ends; an ordinal that stands no longer is no_such_held. Full reference: help("resolve").

held.description: The held line's ordinal, as held() lists it.

act.description: drop the line, or send it again.

tools.name: publication_open
tools.description: The shell's publication.open call, a publication's first step (PUBLISHING): it reads your draft and holds a PANEL for this session — the links on the selected words by set, the count and the price — and writes nothing. Give doc, the published document of yours whose version chain the member joins, or mint, the account a new published document is minted under with the member its first — never both; also names other drafts of yours re-minted beside it. At the doc form the answer's standing says where the draft's base stands: at_head, behind (a newer version stands, named by head), first or superseded_first — told, never refused. Next: publication_count for each answer and switch, then publication_confirm, or publication_cancel to drop the panel. One panel stands at a time. At the doc form, base_unrecorded: the board records no base for the draft in doc's chain — stage a draft from doc and write your text there. Full reference: help("publication_open").

draft.description: The draft of yours whose text the member carries.

also.description: Other private drafts of yours of the same document whose words this publication re-mints as the document's own, each keeping a record of where its words went; never your notes or another document's draft. Each named once, never the draft itself.

doc.description: The published document of yours whose version chain the member joins as its next. Give doc or mint, never both.

mint.description: The account a new published document is minted under in the same write, the member its first: a draft's first publication. Give doc or mint, never both.

claim.description: Carry the edition claim in the same write: with mint, or with a doc that holds no member yet; where a member already stands, confirm answers refused, arm claim_refused. Default false.

selection.description: The text to publish, as runs in V-order; absent, the draft's whole text.

items.description: One run: width positions of origin's content I-space from the ordinal i_start.

origin.description: The document whose content I-space the run lies in: doc, for a run whose first I-address image answers as doc.0.1.ordinal.

i_start.description: The run's first ordinal in origin's content I-space: the last component of that I-address.

notes.description: Your notes documents, in the order their rows stand.

readable_drafts.description: Your drafts the publication reads through, the draft itself joining them. Absent, the board's index lists them, which the open waits on.

published.description: Your published documents: where a link's home counts as published, and where a switched-on row's links may go. Absent, the board's index lists them, which the open waits on.

tools.name: publication_count
tools.description: The shell's publication.count call, the call per answer: re-counts the standing panel under the switches and answers you send, writing nothing (PUBLISHING). switches.on names the private rows to publish, and answers keys each window part "run.part" to its answer. It answers the panel re-keyed by those answers, its count and its price as they would stand: a non-empty price.over is refused over_cap at confirm. The panel keeps what you send here, but publication_confirm reads none of it — send it the switches and answers you settled on. no_panel (isError): no panel stands — publication_open first. malformed_args names answers where a key is no part's or an answer one its part does not admit. Full reference: help("publication_count").

switches.description: The private rows switched on, and where each one's links go.

on.description: The homes of the private rows switched ON; every other private row stays OFF.

destinations.description: Per switched-on home, where its links go: "member", the member the confirm publishes (the default), or {"set": address}, another published document of yours.

answers.description: One answer per window part, keyed "run.part" (the window's run, its index in the selection, and the part's index in the window, each a decimal string), as the part admits: counterpart (the part re-composed by reference to the published words its record names, windowed from the version that published them) or drop (leave the part's words out) where a record names its words; publish_first (publish the window's origin first; this publication stays inert), drop, or keep_private (the member keeps the part as a window onto your unpublished origin: readers see a placeholder) where none does.

tools.name: publication_confirm
tools.description: The shell's publication.confirm call: publishes the standing panel's selection in ONE signed write, composed off the panel and the switches and answers sent here — it reads none of publication_count's: send the ones you settled on (PUBLISHING). It reads the draft and its base again, then answers one outcome, as data. "acknowledged": published, member its address; the panel is gone. "restated": the draft, its base or its standing moved since the panel, nothing sent — open the panel again on the same draft, then confirm again. "refused": nothing published, its arm saying why — over_cap, inert, a window part unanswered, or the board's refusal. no_panel (isError): open first. held_lines (isError): a draft holds a line of yours the board has not kept — call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then confirm again. Answered no_panel or session_died after its session ended, or unreachable, it may still have published: open and confirm again. Full reference: help("publication_confirm").

switches.description: The private rows switched on, and where each one's links go.

on.description: The homes of the private rows switched ON; every other private row stays OFF.

destinations.description: Per switched-on home, where its links go: "member", the member the confirm publishes (the default), or {"set": address}, another published document of yours.

answers.description: One answer per window part, keyed "run.part" (the window's run, its index in the selection, and the part's index in the window, each a decimal string), as the part admits: counterpart (the part re-composed by reference to the published words its record names, windowed from the version that published them) or drop (leave the part's words out) where a record names its words; publish_first (publish the window's origin first; this publication stays inert), drop, or keep_private (the member keeps the part as a window onto your unpublished origin: readers see a placeholder) where none does.

tools.name: publication_cancel
tools.description: The shell's publication.cancel call: drops the standing panel, nothing sent and nothing written (PUBLISHING); a panel held behind it stands. With none standing it answers {} all the same. Response: {}.

tools.name: publication_standing
tools.description: The shell's publication.standing call: where a draft of yours stands against its document before you publish — no panel composed and nothing written (PUBLISHING). Give draft; doc, the published document whose version chain it joins, which a draft's base does not say; and also, as publication_open takes it. Answers {base, standing, head?, left_behind}: base the version its next publication lands after; standing at_head (the member would be the newest version), behind (a newer version stands, named by head: the member would land beside it as the base's daughter), first (no version yet) or superseded_first (version 1 has since been published: the member would land beside it); left_behind the drafts a publication of it would leave behind. base_unrecorded: the board records no base for the draft in doc's chain — stage a draft from doc and write your text there. Full reference: help("publication_standing").

draft.description: The draft of yours whose standing is read.

doc.description: The published document of yours whose version chain the draft joins.

also.description: Other private drafts of yours of the same document a publication of this one would re-mint beside it. Each named once, never the draft itself.

tools.name: merge_compose
tools.description: The shell's merge.compose call: merges a published document's head with ONE side and LANDS the merge in a draft of yours, by one write (MERGING). doc is the document itself, never a version; the side is alternative, a daughter of doc's chain, draft, a draft of doc's owner's account whose recorded base is a version of doc, or fork, another account's document taken from one. M, the merged words at their defaults, lands as the whole of into, or of a fresh draft staged from the head where none is named — name into, so a call made again re-opens it. Answers the report {outcome, gaps, …}: "landed", into and position, your next as_of on into; "reopened", into already carries this merge: nothing landed, each gap read off into as it stands — read into before you write to it; "merged", the daughter is merged already: nothing landed. Settle a gap by EDITING into, then merge_land publishes it. base_unknown and held_lines are isError, nothing written. Full reference: help("merge_compose").

doc.description: The published document merged: the document itself, never a version of it. It needs a published version.

alternative.description: The side: a daughter of doc's chain (doc.k.m), a version published beside a newer one. Give alternative, draft or fork, one alone.

draft.description: The side: a draft of doc's owner's account whose recorded base (doc_metadata(draft).base) is doc or a version of doc. Give alternative, draft or fork, one alone.

fork.description: The side: another account's document standing on doc or a version of doc — its doc_metadata base where the board records one (an agent's stage of one, moved to the head by each landing into it), else its source (an agent's version of one) — composed over the head, its base read up the bases the board recorded from there. A draft of doc's owner's account is refused here, base_unknown with reason fork_of_owner: give it as draft. Give alternative, draft or fork, one alone.

into.description: The unpublished draft of yours the merge lands in, never the draft side itself: best one staged from the head, so a call made again re-opens it. The fork side itself, where it is yours, takes the merge at any head where you staged it, its recorded base moving there, and where a version minted it only where its source is the head — else merge_refused fork_base_moved, nothing written. Absent: a fresh draft is staged from the head.

tools.name: merge_land
tools.description: The shell's merge.land call: publishes the standing merge from the draft it landed in, in ONE signed write through the publication family — a daughter's supersession claim riding in it — then writes the merge record (MERGING). The draft is published as it stands: resolutions, {gap id: choice}, record your choice at each gap and change no words. answers: one per window part, keyed "run.part", as publication_confirm takes them — none is answered for you. Answers {outcome: "landed", member, supersede, daughter, record, …}, the composition gone: a published merge is not undone. "restated": nothing sent — call again. "refused", supersede_refused with head_moved: a newer version stands — compose again on it. window_parts_owed (isError) names every part to answer; no_merge (isError): nothing composed, or the draft no longer carries this merge — compose again. Full reference: help("merge_land").

resolutions.description: Your choice at each gap, keyed by the gap's id as the report names it (a decimal string), recorded in the merge record: it changes no words, so settle a gap by editing the draft first. keep_both keeps the default; omit leaves the gap's runs out; {order: [sides]} places them in that order of sides (0 the head, 1 the side), none twice; {keep_only: side} keeps one side's; {after: anchor} or {before: anchor} names the gap's own after or before anchor.

answers.description: One answer per window part, keyed "run.part" (the window's run, its index in the selection, and the part's index in the window, each a decimal string), as the part admits: counterpart (the part re-composed by reference to the published words its record names, windowed from the version that published them) or drop (leave the part's words out) where a record names its words; publish_first (publish the window's origin first; this publication stays inert), drop, or keep_private (the member keeps the part as a window onto your unpublished origin: readers see a placeholder) where none does.

tools.name: merge_undo
tools.description: The shell's merge.undo call: takes the standing merge's landing back out of its draft in ONE write, the words and merge marker the draft held before it put back (MERGING); merge_undo(draft, withdrawal) instead puts back a merge merge_withdraw took out, withdrawal its answer's position. It lands only where nothing changed the draft since that write — your own edits included: past any change it is refused arrangement_moved (data), nothing changed, and the undo can no longer land — keep the words and take the merge out with merge_withdraw. Answers {draft, position, record, restored, marker?}: position your next as_of on draft. no_merge (isError): no merge stands to undo — merge_land published it, or this adapter's session ended. nothing_to_undo {draft, why} and held_lines are isError, nothing sent. Full reference: help("merge_undo").

draft.description: The draft a merge was withdrawn from, given with withdrawal. Absent with withdrawal absent: the standing landing taken back.

withdrawal.description: The position merge_withdraw answered for the draft: given with draft, the withdrawal put back. Absent with draft absent: the standing landing taken back.

tools.name: merge_withdraw
tools.description: The shell's merge.withdraw call: takes the merge out of a draft of yours and KEEPS its words, in ONE write: the draft's merge marker is cleared, so a publication of it claims no daughter superseded (MERGING). It takes any marked draft of yours, in any session. Answers {draft, position, record}: position your next as_of on draft, and the withdrawal's handle — merge_undo(draft, withdrawal: position) puts the merge back while nothing changed the draft since. refused arrangement_moved (data): the draft changed while it was read, nothing changed — call again. no_merge (isError): the draft carries no merge; not_owner and held_lines are isError, nothing sent. Full reference: help("merge_withdraw").

draft.description: The draft of yours whose merge is taken out, its words kept.

tools.name: session_info
tools.description: Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: who you are at this board — {principal, account (your principal's account: a principal the board seats no account for stops this adapter at startup), key: {fingerprint, label} (the store's key as the adapter selected it at its start, enrolled in the account's set or the nearest set above it; a key bound into the store since then signs from the next session the shell opens, which this answer does not name), board (the origin), writes (whether this session may write), another_window (present, true, only while another shell over this adapter's --dir — a running dev provider's — holds the board's held store: every write is refused another_window then, nothing sent and nothing held, though writes stays true; stop the other and start this adapter again), mode (UNCLAIMED, CLAIMED-PERMISSIVE or ENFORCING) and health (the board's GET /health answer verbatim, log_position among its members)}. Call it first.

tools.name: changes_since
tools.description: The shell's changes call as a pull: what changed on the board since the log position since, at your reader class (WHAT CHANGED). Answers {entries, next, head}: entries the /changes rows, oldest first, each with its position, op, docs and hand; next the position to ask from next time — keep it, and pass it as since; head the board's latest position. Start from session_info's health.log_position, or from 0 for everything. class "drafts" reads the rows of the drafts you may read alone; under, an address, narrows every read to the rows at or under it — one draft's history — and its next is the narrowed feed's: keep one next per under. A since below the board's memory is refused history_reclaimed, naming the floor: ask again from it. Full reference: help("changes_since").

since.description: The log position to read from: the page is (since, head].

limit.description: At most this many entries (the board's default, 256, when absent).

class.description: Narrow the page to the drafts rows alone: the entries naming a draft you may read, nothing published. Absent, both classes are merged by position.

under.description: Narrow the page to the rows naming a document at or under this address — a draft, a document or an account. Keep the next it answers apart from an unnarrowed one.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The bytes of the picture whose reference cell sits at the I-address i (doc.0.1.ordinal), fetched whole under your session and checked by the board against the cell's hash and size. The result is one content block: an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) where the bytes' magic names one — the type sniffed here, never attested — else an embedded resource blob of application/octet-stream. A file past this adapter's cap of 8 MiB, or a stream cut short, is isError, its text a plain sentence (FETCH); a file you may not read is withheld; a cell that is none is not_a_cell. Full reference: help("fetch").

i.description: The I-address the cell sits at, as insert's ack_addr named it.

tools.name: replace_text
tools.description: Adapter apparatus: replaces one exact text with another in a draft you own, rewriting only the bytes that differ, so every other byte keeps its identity and the links on it. Several changes at once: edit_text; whole lines moved: move_lines. The first text of an empty draft, words placed by identity: insert, copy, set_arrangement. old must stand EXACTLY ONCE in the draft — quote enough text around your change to make it so; an empty new removes old; pass no as_of. Answers one object by outcome. "replaced": landed, its at the as_of your next burst on doc is typed against. "unchanged": old and new are the same text. "refused": nothing of the edit stands and no line is held — not_unique: quote more text; not_found: read the draft; arrangement_moved: the draft changed under the call — call again. "partial" and "held" are isError: part of the edit stands, or may — read the draft before you edit it again, after resolve on a held line (HELD BURSTS). Full reference: help("replace_text").

doc.description: The draft whose text is edited (a draft you own). A published document, or a member of one, is refused published.

old.description: The text to replace, exactly as the draft holds it, UTF-8: it must stand exactly once in the draft's text. Quote the text around your change with it where the changed words alone stand more than once — what old and new share at either end is left untouched.

new.description: The text to stand in old's place, UTF-8; empty removes old.

tools.name: edit_text
tools.description: Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: several edits of a draft you own in ONE call, answered with the lines they changed. Call edit_text(doc, edits: [{old, new}, …]): each old must stand EXACTLY ONCE in the draft as the pairs before it leave it, and new stands in its place, an empty new removing old; at most 4096 pairs. ALL OR NOTHING: every pair is checked against one read before anything is written, and a write that does not land sets the draft back. Each pair is made as its smallest changes, so the text between keeps its identity. One change: replace_text. A landed call answers "edited" on line 1, its at the as_of your next burst on doc is typed against, then the lines it changed, one row a line, numbered as line_numbers counts lines. "refused": nothing stands, pair naming the pair refused — not_unique: quote more of the text. partial and held are isError: part of the call stands, or may — read the draft before you edit it again. Full reference: help("edit_text").

doc.description: The draft whose text is edited (a draft you own). A published document, or a member of one, is refused published.

edits.description: The pairs, made in order: each old is found exactly once in the draft as the pairs before it leave it. One wire list, at most 4096 entries.

items.description: One pair: old, the text to replace, and new, the text to stand in its place.

old.description: The text to replace, exactly as the draft holds it once the pairs before it are made, UTF-8: it must stand exactly once there. Quote the text around a change where the changed words alone stand more than once.

new.description: The text to stand in old's place, UTF-8; empty removes old.

tools.name: move_lines
tools.description: Adapter apparatus: moves whole lines of a draft you own, in ONE call, by identity — no byte is retyped, so every byte keeps its identity and its links. Use it to move a block: lines retyped (edit_text) are minted anew and lose their links, and rearrange asks for byte positions. Call move_lines(doc, first, last?, before?): lines first to last, both included (last absent: the one line), move to stand before line before (absent: the end). Lines count from 1, as line_numbers counts them: take them from a read or answer made after your last change. The lines move exactly as given: to carry a blank line, include it. It answers "moved" on line 1 — to_first and to_last where the lines now stand, at your next as_of on doc — then the lines moved and the place they left, one row a line. "refused": nothing moved — no_such_line: read the draft; arrangement_moved: the draft changed under the call: read it, then call again. held is isError (HELD BURSTS). Full reference: help("move_lines").

doc.description: The draft whose lines are moved (a draft you own). A published document, or a member of one, is refused published.

first.description: The first line of the block, numbered from 1 as line_numbers counts lines.

last.description: The last line of the block, itself moved. Absent, the block is the one line first.

before.description: The line the block is to stand before, a line outside the block. Absent, or one past the last line, the block moves to the end of the text.

tools.name: mark_text
tools.description: Adapter apparatus: marks a draft, in ONE call — a private document of your account that holds the draft's whole content by identity, to diff against later. Nothing is read or typed anew: the mark holds the draft's very bytes, and one link typed marks, homed in the mark, says which draft it marks. Use it before work you will review: mark, change the draft, then diff_text(doc, since: the mark) shows what you changed. Call mark_text(doc). It answers "marked": mark, the new document's address, to pass as since; link, the marks link; at, its commit. A mark is kept among your documents. "refused": no mark was made — where it names mark, that is the empty document the call left. partial is isError: the copy stands and is usable as since, with no marks link. held is isError (HELD BURSTS). Full reference: help("mark_text").

doc.description: The draft to mark: a document you may read, whose whole content the mark holds by identity.

tools.name: diff_text
tools.description: Adapter apparatus: shows what changed in a draft since an earlier state of it, BY IDENTITY, in ONE call that writes nothing. Use it before you hand work on, instead of reading the draft back: a block moved shows as moved, not deleted and added, and text deleted and typed again is said re-typed, which a text diff hides. Call diff_text(doc, since, stat?, hunk?): since is a mark (mark_text), the version the draft was staged from, or a document it copied from; stat: true answers the byte counts alone; hunk goes on from next_hunk. It answers "diffed" on line 1 — shared, bytes, lines, notes — then the hunks, one row a line: " N" unchanged, "-N" gone, "+N" new, ">N" a line moved here with its identity kept, "<" where moved lines left. "unchanged": nothing changed. shared "0": since shares nothing with the draft — check since. "refused", arrangement_moved: the draft kept changing — call again. Words a publication re-minted pair with since: only edits show. Full reference: help("diff_text").

doc.description: The draft whose changes are shown.

since.description: The document the draft is compared with, whose content the draft holds by identity: a mark of it (mark_text), the version member it was staged from, or a document it copied from.

stat.description: True answers the counts alone — shared and bytes — and reads no text. Absent, false.

hunk.description: The hunk the rows start at, from 1: an earlier answer's next_hunk. Absent, the first.

tools.name: restore_text
tools.description: Adapter apparatus: puts a draft you own back as it stood at an earlier position, in ONE write, BY IDENTITY: the old words come back as the very bytes they were, their links with them, where retyped text is minted anew. It takes back EVERY change made since at, yours and any other hand's. Call restore_text(draft, at, as_of): at, a position the draft stood at — the as_of of a read made before the change, an earlier edit's at, or the at of a changes_since(under: draft) row; as_of, your typed state (THE TYPED STATE), never session_info's log_position. Answers {draft, at, position, as_of, marker}: position the write's commit, your next as_of on draft; restore_text(draft, at: as_of, as_of: position) is the way back. refused arrangement_moved is data: the draft changed past your as_of, nothing changed — read it, then call again at that read's as_of. merge_refused (not_past, history_reclaimed, not_a_position) and held_lines are isError, nothing sent. Full reference: help("restore_text").

draft.description: The draft put back: a draft you own. A published document is refused not_owner, published.

at.description: The position whose state of the draft is made current: one the draft stood at before the change — a read's as_of, an earlier edit's at, or a changes_since(under: draft) row's at.

as_of.description: Your typed state of the draft: the as_of of your last read of it or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later.

tools.name: help
tools.description: Adapter apparatus, needing no board: the catalog's help. help() lists the topics, one a line — headings in capitals, then tools. help(topic) answers one topic's text: a heading the instructions or a card name in parentheses, as (HELD BURSTS), or a tool whose card ends naming its full reference. A topic it does not hold is isError, naming the topics.

topic.description: The topic to read: a heading in capitals ("HELD BURSTS") or a tool's name ("replace_text"). Absent, help answers the list of topics.

help.text: OVERVIEW. skep is a substrate of documents, immutable content, and first-class links, served by the skepd daemon. You reach one board through this adapter, which runs the shell's core within it (skep-shell, the engine a person's desktop shell runs on; "the shell" below), under ONE SIGNED SESSION it opened at startup for your principal, with your principal's key: every write you make goes out under that session and is attributed to your account forever. A publish-class write — a published document minted, a member published, a write into a published document — carries that key's own signature (its /changes entry's attest); every other carries the board's testimony that your session made it (the entry's key, that key's fingerprint). Tools come in two kinds. A WIRE OPERATION tool (create_new_document, insert, make_link, retrieve_v, image, ...) is one operation of the wire: its name is the frame's op, its arguments are the frame, and its result text is the board's answer to the frame as JSON — the response document, tagged by resp — save a burst the shell holds, whose text is its held answer (HELD BURSTS), and a frame refused, by the board or by the shell before it sends it, whose text is the refusal (REJECTIONS ARE DATA). The other tools are the shell's own calls — search, places, held, resolve, boards, health, probe, publication_standing, where a draft stands against its document with no panel composed, and the four of a publication, publication_open, publication_count, publication_confirm and publication_cancel, which stand in for the wire's publish (PUBLISHING), and the four of a merge, merge_compose, merge_land, merge_undo and merge_withdraw, which land a published document's head merged with one side in a draft of yours and publish it (MERGING) — and this adapter's apparatus: session_info, changes_since (the shell's changes, as a pull), fetch (the shell's fetch, as a content block), replace_text (a text edit of a draft, composed of the reads and the bursts above), edit_text (several such edits in one call, all landing or none, answered with the lines they changed), move_lines (whole lines of a draft moved by identity, by one rearrange, answered with the lines where they now stand), mark_text (a private copy of a draft's content by identity, to diff against later), diff_text (what changed in a draft since such a document, by identity, a move shown as a move) and restore_text (a draft put back as it stood at an earlier position, in one write by identity: EDITING TEXT).

WHO YOU ARE. Call session_info first. It reports your principal, your account, the key you sign with (its fingerprint and label), the board, writes (whether this session may write), another_window where another shell holds the board's held store (every write refused, though writes stays true), and the board's health with its mode and log_position. You cannot run key or claim ceremonies here — there is no keygen, enroll, rotate, retire, claim, handoff, accept or recover: those are your person's, at their own client. Your person stops you by retiring your key, and this adapter then stops.

FIND BEFORE YOU WRITE. search(query) finds passages by their words at your reader class (what your session may read); places() lists every document you may read, each with its first line; find_links_v and find_links_ftt find the links on a region or by their slots. Read state on every search and places answer: while state.arm is none or building (or busy), the index is not yet built from the board, so a miss is not absence — ask again later, or read the documents directly. Link or transclude, never retype: cite another's passage with make_link, or transclude it with copy, which shares its identity. Publish, never rewrite: a published document is never edited in place; stage the change in a draft and publish it as the next member of its chain (PUBLISHING).

YOUR DOCUMENTS. Your account's first document is your PUBLISHED HOME, doc 1, born published: an insert into it is refused published_target — and held, as every burst the board rejects is, until you resolve it (HELD BURSTS). Mint a second document with create_new_document(account) for your text; it is a DRAFT: yours to write, read by you and by whoever the board's read predicate admits — among them the accounts above yours and beneath it, and a grant's holders — and a draft for life, since no document's publication ever changes. To publish a draft's text is to append it to a published document's chain as its next member, born published, or to mint a published document in the same write with the member its first — and the draft stays a draft, yours to stage the next change in (PUBLISHING). search and places call a published document an EDITION: they answer its kind as edition, a draft's as draft.

EDITING TEXT. To change a draft's text, call replace_text(doc, old, new): it finds the exact text old, which must stand once in the draft, and replaces only the bytes in which new differs from it, so every other byte keeps its identity and the links on it follow — where a line retyped through insert and delete, or a whole text set afresh, is minted anew and leaves every link on the old words behind. It reads the draft itself and types its writes against that read, so you count no position and pass no as_of; a draft that changed under it answers refused, arrangement_moved, nothing of the edit standing and no line held, and you call again. Its answer is one object by outcome — replaced, unchanged, refused, or, each isError, partial and held, which name what stands — and help("replace_text") says each. To make several changes at once, call edit_text(doc, edits), edits a list of {old, new} pairs made in order, each old standing once in the draft as the pairs before it leave it: every pair is checked against one read before anything is written, all of them land or none, each is made as its smallest changes, and a landed call answers with the lines it changed, numbered, so you need not read the draft back to see your edit. To move whole lines, call move_lines(doc, first, last?, before?): the lines first to last move to stand before the line before, or at the end of the text, by identity — no byte is retyped, so every link on them follows, where lines removed and typed again leave their links behind — and a landed call answers with the lines where they now stand. To review your own work, call mark_text(doc) before you change a draft and diff_text(doc, since) before you hand it on, since the mark: the diff shows what changed by identity — moved lines as moved, text typed again as re-typed — with no need to read the draft back. To put a draft back as it stood at an earlier position, call restore_text(draft, at, as_of): one write, by identity, so the old words come back with the links on them — it takes back every change made since at, and its answer names the way back. insert, delete, copy, reinstate, rearrange and set_arrangement stay yours where a change is neither old text for new nor whole lines moved: the first text of an empty draft, words placed by identity, a move that is not whole lines. A published document takes none of them (PUBLISHING).

PUBLISHING. A publication is ONE signed write the shell composes for you from a draft, and no tool sends a publish of yours: stage the text in a draft, then publication_open(draft, doc) — doc the published document whose chain the member joins — or publication_open(draft, mint) — mint the account a new published document is minted under, the member its first. Stage a draft for a document's chain with stage(from_) — from_ the version you stage the change to, the document itself while it has no version yet, or another draft of yours for an alternative of it: in one write the board mints the draft holding from_'s words by identity and records its BASE, the version its next publication lands after, moving it to the member each publication of the draft makes; doc_metadata(draft) answers it as base, and there is no record for you to write. The shell reads the draft's base itself, from the board, and nothing of the base is yours to send: the member lands after that version, or as its daughter beside the latest where the chain has moved on — or, for a draft begun before any version, as version 1's daughter — never over newer words; a draft the board records no base for — one you minted with create_new_document or fork rather than staged — is refused base_unrecorded, and a mint, which starts a chain, needs none. publication_standing(draft, doc) answers the base and where it stands — the newest version named where it is behind — with no panel composed. The open holds the PANEL and answers it: rows, the links on the selected words by set, a private set's links left out until switches.on names its row; the count and the price; and windows, runs whose words another unpublished draft of yours holds, each in parts that need their own answers, a part whose words a record names as already published taking counterpart or drop — a window awaiting its answer counts toward nothing. publication_count(switches, answers), the call per answer, answers the panel re-keyed by the answers with the count and the price as they would stand. publication_confirm(switches, answers), sent the switches and answers you settled on, reads the draft again and answers one outcome, as data: acknowledged, with the member's address, the panel gone; restated, the draft moved since the panel, or the board refused an entry already carrying its copy and the panel left it out, and nothing sent — read the panel again (publication_open on the same draft) and confirm again; or refused, nothing published, with its arm. publication_cancel drops the panel. One panel stands at a time, and it lives with the session it was opened under: once that session ends — a board restart among the causes, this adapter's next session opened silently — count and confirm answer no_panel, and you open it again. A confirm answered no_panel or session_died after its session ended, or unreachable, may still have published: open and confirm again — where it landed, the draft's words are the member's own, and the new confirm answers refused, arm inert, its inert unchanged. On the wire the publish may also carry supersede, the daughters a merged version takes in — version members of the document's own chain — each a supersession claim signed in the same write and homed in the document, so in_claims at the daughter answers it: publication_open over a draft whose merge marker names the trunk's head composes them as count.supersede, the daughters the marker names, and the merge tools land such a merge in a draft of yours and publish it (MERGING).

MERGING. A merge joins a published document's head with ONE side — a version published beside a newer one, a draft of yours behind the head, or another account's fork of a version — and lands the joined words in a draft of yours, to settle and publish as the next version with its supersession claim and its merge record. What a merge takes: doc, the document itself, never a version of it, with a published version — a document never published has nothing to merge — whose head, its newest version, the shell reads; and ONE side: alternative, a daughter of doc's chain, doc.k.m — a version published beside a newer one, as a publication that raced lands — or draft, a draft of doc's owner's account whose recorded base (doc_metadata(draft).base) is doc or a version of doc: a draft staged from doc or from a version, or from a draft of yours staged that way; or fork, another account's document whose recorded base (doc_metadata(fork).base), else its source (doc_metadata(fork).source), is doc or a version of doc — its stage or version of one; a landing into a fork staged so moves its base, and the fork is merged from where it now stands. The base is read off the bases the board recorded, never off an address: a side begun from doc before its first version — a draft or a fork still unpublished, or a daughter published beside version 1 — composes over doc as it stood before version 1, empty on most documents, base then doc itself, and the texts written apart meet in an order gap you settle by editing into, as at any gap; while doc has no version yet it is refused base_unknown with reason bare_source, nothing to merge onto — publish that draft, which lands version 1. A draft never staged, one staged from a draft with no recorded base, and one of another account — give that one as fork — are refused base_unknown, nothing written, as is a fork whose recorded base, else its source, is neither doc nor a version of it; a draft of doc's owner's account given as fork is refused base_unknown with reason fork_of_owner — give it as draft — for a fork is another account's document, and the owner's draft's words are re-minted only at the draft side; reason hop_unrecorded names the hop, a version on the side's line the board records no base for. A fork composed by its own owner lands in a fresh draft of theirs staged from the head, re-basing it there for doc's owner to merge. merge_compose(doc, alternative | draft | fork, into?) WRITES: it lands M, the merged words at their defaults, as the whole arrangement of into — an unpublished draft of yours, best one staged from the head — or of a fresh draft staged from the head where none is named, by one write, and answers the report: outcome landed, into, position (the landing's commit, your next as_of on into) and the gaps. Composing again answers reopened — into already carries this merge (save at a fork changed since the landing: that merge is composed again on the head and LANDS over into, replacing the earlier landing's words and your edits since, and replaced names each stretch it replaced — merge_undo puts them back): nothing landed, each gap's state read off into as it stands, position the first landing's, so read into before you write to it — or merged, the daughter merged already by a claim of yours: member the version that merged it, its record beside it, nothing landed. The gaps: each a spot both sides changed, by kind — order, corner, cut, collision and moves are unsettled, each left at a default; anchor is settled by the rules — its runs named by side, 0 for the head and 1 for the side. A gap is settled by EDITING THE DRAFT: remove a side's runs whole, or reorder them, and compose again, which reads the gap settled, resolved_by agent; an edit inside a run's words settles nothing. merge_land(resolutions?, answers?) publishes the draft as it stands through the publication family's one signed write (PUBLISHING), the supersession claim on the daughter riding in it — none at the draft or fork side, whose side is no version of doc — then writes the merge record; resolutions record your choice at each gap, {gap id: choice}, and change no words. It answers NO window part for you: until every window part is answered in answers, keyed "run.part", it is refused window_parts_owed, every part named. It answers restated, nothing sent: call again; refused, supersede_refused with detail head_moved — the race, a newer version published since the compose: compose again on the head it names; and, at the draft or fork side, daughter true where the head moved under the shot and the member landed beside it. A panel of yours over the draft that mints an edition or publishes into another document refuses it other_panel: publication_cancel that panel — a held one first opened again in its own form, publication_open with the draft and the doc or mint the refusal names and nothing else — then merge_land again. merge_land publishes into doc, which only its owner can. After a landing the composition is gone, and merge_undo answers no_merge: a published merge is not undone. The composition lives with this adapter's session: after a board restart the next session holds none, and merge_land and merge_undo answer no_merge — compose again, which re-opens into. A merge_land answered session_died or unreachable, or no_merge after a session's end, may still have published: at a daughter, compose it again — merged names the member; at the draft or fork side, doc_metadata(into).base names the version it published. A merge_compose answered unreachable, or one that met the end of this adapter's session — which the adapter makes again itself, once — may have left a draft it staged, or landed in, that no merge record names: name into, so a call made again re-opens it, or lands there, and stages nothing more. With none named, a call — the adapter's own once included — that finds the merge landed in such a draft is refused merge_refused landing_begun {draft, position}, nothing staged or written, never a second landing: compose again naming draft as into, before you write to it, which re-opens it and writes its record; then merge_undo() takes the merge back, or merge_withdraw(draft) takes it out and keeps its words. A draft only staged, the merge never landed in it, is found by its stage row on changes_since(class: "drafts") from before the call. Taking it back: merge_undo() takes the landing back by one write only where nothing changed the draft since the landing, your own edits included — you have no editor's stack that takes them back first: past any change it is refused arrangement_moved, nothing changed. merge_withdraw(draft) takes the merge out of any draft of yours and keeps its words, and merge_undo(draft, withdrawal) puts it back. A withdrawal, or its undo, whose write landed before a session's end has taken effect: read doc_metadata(draft).merge before you compose again. arrangement_moved is data, the board's verdict, nothing changed; base_unknown {side, reason}, nothing_to_undo {draft, why}, window_parts_owed, other_panel, held_lines {doc, held}, not_owner and no_merge are isError, the shell's own, nothing sent. Each tool's whole reference: help("merge_compose"), help("merge_land"), help("merge_undo"), help("merge_withdraw").

ENCODINGS. Tumblers and addresses are dotted-decimal strings ("1.0.1.0.1.0.1.1"), zeros explicit. Spell each component without a leading zero: the shell refuses any other spelling of a burst's doc, fetch's i and places' under. Unbounded naturals (widths, V-position components) are decimal strings ("5"); non-negative integers are accepted. Log positions (at/as_of), slots, window sizes, and principal ids are plain JSON numbers. Spans are {"start": <tumbler>, "width": <tumbler>}, half-open in the tumbler order; zero-width is invalid; the depth-2 content V-span {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} names subspace 1 (content), ordinal 1, five positions. V-positions are {"subspace", "ordinal"} naturals; subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based. Content granularity is said, never fallen into: in insert's values array, a bare string mints one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte ("hello" is five values at five positions) and {"hex"} one per raw byte; {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} mint ONE composite value at ONE position whose interior is permanently unaddressable — no link, transclusion, or compare can ever reach inside it. Deliveries are injective: a maximal run of single-byte values renders as one {"content"} item ({"hex"} when the run is not UTF-8), each composite value as its own {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} item, and a link position as {"ref"}. Count positions, not items: {"content": "hello"} spans five positions, {"atom": "hello"} one.

REJECTIONS ARE DATA. An operation the board refuses — save a burst the shell holds instead (HELD BURSTS) — is a normal tool result (isError false) whose text is {"kind": "refused", "name", "status", "code", "detail", "op", "body"}: body is the board's verdict verbatim — {"resp": "rejected", "op", "code", "disposition", ...} for an operation, or a route's non-200 {"error", ...} body — and name is the one token to act on. Where the shell reads the board to compose the attest of a write it signs — create_new_document, fork, version, insert, make_link, emit, nullify, assert_sup or edit_link, into a draft as into a published document — the board's refusal of that read is the answer, as data, its op the read's (image, retrieve_doc_v_span_set or retrieve_v), and the write was not sent. A publication the board refuses, or the shell refuses before it sends it, is publication_confirm's own outcome, refused, as data (PUBLISHING). disposition is advisory: permanent (reissuing the same request cannot succeed), reorder (a future committed state may satisfy the precondition; reissue after it commits), retry (transient; the operation did nothing), halt (writes stopped; reads still work). Two answers that are data may still have committed: a write refused poisoned may land when the board restarts, its frames standing in the journal the restart replays, and a write answered internal_panic (a 500) may have committed before the daemon's handler failed. After either, read what it wrote (or changes_since, once the board answers) before you send it again. isError true means the shell could not get the board's verdict, and its text is a refusal of another kind: unreachable (the board is not answering), halt (a face with state, cause and act — attest_not_composed where the shell could not compose the attest of a write it signs: nothing was sent, and where its state names one of your arguments, fix that one; head_unreadable where the board's head record (H.1), which the attest of a write it signs names, stands and cannot be read — a garbled answer from the board's head record among its causes — or a claimed board serves none: nothing was sent, the record is the board's to repair, and a burst so refused is held instead, HELD BURSTS), blocked, or shell (the shell's own, by name: malformed_args naming an argument of the wrong form, frame_too_large, session_ended, session_died, query_too_long, no_panel, base_unrecorded, held_lines {doc, held} — a publication_confirm over a draft holding lines of yours the board has not kept, the rendering draft or one named also, a restore_text whose draft holds them, or a merge tool over a draft that does — merge_compose's into or the draft a merge record of yours names, merge_land's draft or draft side, merge_undo's and merge_withdraw's draft — nothing sent: call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then call again — ...) — save this adapter's own answers, whose text is a plain sentence: fetch's two (FETCH), and help's answer to a topic it holds no text for. The shell refuses some wire-operation frames itself, before it sends them, nothing sent: its malformed_args names a wire operation's argument as frame.<argument> — a burst's doc must be a document address, and its id may not begin shell:, the prefix of the ids the shell resends a held burst under — and frame_too_large is a burst whose frame would pass the board's cap. Every write is refused another_window, nothing sent and nothing held, while another shell over this adapter's --dir — a running dev provider's — holds the board's held store: session_info says so, another_window true, and this process reads alone at that board, so stop the other and start this adapter again. A call answered session_died met the end of the session this adapter holds, its reason beside it, and ran nothing — save a publication_confirm, which may have sent its request first (PUBLISHING), and the merge tools, merge_compose, merge_land, merge_undo and merge_withdraw, each of which may have written before the end (MERGING): unless that end stops the adapter — your key retired, your prefix blocked — call again, and the next call opens a session afresh; a halt named busy is a sign-in the board did not accept this time, and its act is try again. The shell reissues within a call exactly what the wire says to reissue — write_busy once, durability twice — and never more, on every write it sends by the op path: a wire operation's, and each a text tool sends. restore_text sends its one write once: a write_busy or durability it meets is its answer, as data, the write not made — call again. A write refused unreachable may still have committed: its frame may have reached the board before its answer was lost, and nothing here reissues it — read what it wrote (or changes_since) before you send it again. Any other write that answers isError did not commit, a publication_confirm's (PUBLISHING) and a merge tool's (MERGING) aside; a burst the board cannot take, or rejects, answers held instead, as data (HELD BURSTS). Every write acknowledgment carries at (the commit that made it true); every read carries as_of (its snapshot).

THE TYPED STATE. Every burst — an insert, delete, copy, reinstate or rearrange — carries as_of, REQUIRED: the position of the document state you typed it against, which is the as_of of your last read of that document (retrieve_v, image, retrieve_doc_v_span_set, line_numbers) or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later; a burst without it is malformed. The board keeps, per document, the position its arrangement last changed at, and refuses a burst typed against an older state arrangement_moved — a permanent refusal carrying site.as_of (yours, echoed) and site.current (that change's position), judged ahead of every position check, so a stale burst never lands off and never answers out_of_bounds for positions that were true when you typed. A burst from the page carries beside its frame the identities on either side of the span it edits and, for a delete or a rearrange, those of the units the span holds (its anchors), and the shell shifts such a burst through the change and sends it again where the change sat wholly elsewhere — every position moved by one displacement, nothing landing off; these tools carry no anchors, so an agent's stale burst is HELD as a document that moved under you (HELD BURSTS), as it is now: its cause moved, held() listing the board's verdict beside it as refusal; resolve its line (drop it), read the document again, place your text against what it holds now, and send it afresh typed at that read's as_of. A link write of yours homed in the document moves nothing: your next burst typed before it still lands.

HELD BURSTS.
