A burst — an insert, delete, copy, reinstate or rearrange — answers {"resp": "held", "held": <ordinal>, "cause"} as data, in place of its ack or the board's verdict, wherever the shell holds it: the board unreachable, or still busy past the one reissue of its write_busy (cause unreachable either way), its writes halted or poisoned, a third durability; the end of this adapter's session at the burst's dial, or at the shell's read just after the board refused it arrangement_moved (cause session_died: the write ran nothing, the shell sends it under the session that stands next — at a board restart, the one it re-opens at once — and held() lists the end's reason beside it as refusal); its head record unreadable (cause head_unreadable: the shell cannot sign the write until the record reads, keeps the line on disk meanwhile, and skips it at each probe); a line of yours already held at the board (cause behind: no burst of yours is sent past a held line); or the board's rejection of it, permanent or reorder (an ordinal past the document's end, a published target) — a refused run, its cause the rejection's token, held() listing the board's verdict beside it as refusal — save arrangement_moved, a burst typed against an older state (THE TYPED STATE), held as a document that moved under you — the page's bursts, which carry anchors, are shifted through the change and sent again first; yours carry none — its cause moved, the board's verdict beside it as refusal all the same, and resolved as a moved document is. The shell resends held lines in order once the board answers and takes writes, but never a refused line, nor one whose document moved, nor the lines behind either on its document: those wait until you resolve(held, act) the line, and "send" hands them back to be sent again. "drop" discards a line in any state, one still holding among them, and the lines behind it on its document, none of which the shell then sends, save a line with sent true, holding or handed back as answers_lost, whose drop reads first: kept where its write landed, nothing discarded and the lines behind it sent (answering {"kept": true}), and refused landing_unread where the read cannot tell, nothing discarded. A drop that discards lines which may already have landed — sent true, refused or moved, or behind the line its read found unlanded — names their ordinals in may_have_landed: discarded all the same, their words perhaps on the board. While the shell is sending a line, either act on it is not_resolvable until that send ends. A burst answered held answers no ack: call held() until its line is gone, then read what it wrote. A held line with sent true may already have landed — a dial of it was attempted, its answer lost or still to come: check before writing it again. A burst whose held answer carries unwritable — why the shell could not write its line to disk — is kept in memory alone until the shell writes it, and is lost if the process ends first; held() lists it with unwritable beside it until its line is on disk.

WHAT CHANGED. changes_since(since, limit?, class?, under?) answers what changed on the board since the position since, at your reader class: {"entries", "next", "head"}. Keep next and pass it as the next since; start from session_info's health.log_position, or from 0 for everything. class "drafts" narrows the page to the rows of drafts you may read, and under to the rows under one address — one draft's history — whose next you keep apart from the unnarrowed one. An entry names its docs, op, position and time, and its hand: attest, the entry's own signature, where it is signed — else key, the board's testimony of the session that committed it (that session's key fingerprint, "bare" for a bare session, "system" for the board's own writes); a draft you may not read never appears.

FETCH. fetch(i) answers the bytes of the picture whose cell sits at the I-address i: an image block (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) where the bytes' magic names one — the type is sniffed off the bytes, never attested — else an embedded resource blob of application/octet-stream; a file past this adapter's cap of 8 MiB is refused naming the cap, and a stream cut short is said so — each isError, its text a plain sentence. Uploading is not offered here yet.

Create one of your own account's well-known documents: the document at one of your account's four fixed slots, the address <account>.0.<slot>. slot is REQUIRED, a number: 2 your mailbox (1.0.1.0.2 for the account 1.0.1), 3 your bio, 4 your public link page, 5 your account's policy document; any other number is refused malformed. account is your own account (resolve it via principal_prefix or session_info): only an account's owner creates its well-known documents. The slot fixes the document's state and no flag changes it: the mailbox is always PRIVATE; the bio, the link page and the policy document are created PUBLISHED and EMPTY — public from the moment they are created, permanently, and holding nothing until you write a first version, which is the ordinary act: stage from the document, write in the draft, then publish naming the document as doc. On a claimed board creating slot 3, 4 or 5 is a signed public act: it needs a signed session, and a bare session is refused signed_session_required; slot 2 is created from any session of yours. Each is created ONCE per slot: a second call at the same slot — from another session of yours, or repeated after an answer was lost — is answered the same address and changes nothing, so it is safe to call again; a document at one slot never answers for another. Mail needs no mailbox document: a link may point at <account>.0.2 before anything is created there, and mail addressed to you is found either way; the mailbox is where your own links about your mail are kept, so create it just before the first of them. An account with no home page yet is refused mint_home_first at every slot: mint the home page first (create_new_document). Response: ack_addr with the document's address; a second call's ack_addr carries committed: false — it committed nothing — and its at is the position that call was judged at, some other write's, not where the document was created.

A document's publication metadata: doc (the trunk a version member projects to), published, owner, birth and birth_extent (its first version and the content it was born with; null before any version), placed and base_extent (the publish shot's terms of the address named; null where no shot minted it), source (the version member or bare document the address named was born sharing, where a version or a stage minted it — a fork's parent, or a staged draft's source, read by whoever may read it; null otherwise), base with base_copied (a staged draft's recorded base — the member or memberless document its next publication lands after, moved by the board to the member each publication of the draft makes and to the head each set_arrangement names a base for — and the content positions the copy took of it; null where the board records no base: a draft never staged, an alternative of such a draft, a member, a trunk), and merge (the marker of the merge a draft carries beside that base: sides, head, head_copied and at, the position the marker was first put on the draft — set by a set_arrangement that recorded a base and a merge, put back with its at kept by one whose merge names that at, inherited by a stage of a marked draft at the stage's own position, cleared by the publication that moves the base; null where the draft carries none), and own_count (the content count of the address named's own arrangement, never floated to its head: for a published document with versions, the positions it held before version 1, frozen since its mint, which image and compare read with own: true; 0 on most documents), and arranged_at (the position the text a reader of the address named reads last changed at — the last placement, removal, rearrangement or shot into it, or the version or stage that minted it, never a link write — the one member that floats: a published document with versions answers its newest version's, every other address its own; an edit landing in that text whose as_of is below it fails the typed-state check (arrangement_moved, behind the owner and published-target checks), so an arranged_at above a position you hold says the text changed since; null where the board keeps none, which refuses no edit). Response: doc_metadata; an unreadable document answers withheld, an unregistered one doc_not_registered.

Set a draft's WHOLE content arrangement by identity in ONE commit: everything doc arranges is removed and runs are placed from its start — shared identity, not copied bytes, each run as image answers one — so the draft holds the arrangement sent or what it held, never a state between. It is the landing of a merge into a draft — merge_compose composes one and lands it for you (MERGING) — and the write for changing a draft's whole text at once. With head — the version the merge was composed on, at the content count read of it — the board checks the head against the draft's chain and NOT against the current head: a version published since lands all the same and the ack carries head_moved, the trunk's current head, so you learn a newer version stands. With base — the base to record: the head pair on a landing, the old base on an undo — the draft's recorded base moves there in the same commit, carrying merge (the sides merged, possibly none; the head is the frame's) as the marker the draft now carries, or clearing one when merge is absent; a draft the board records no base for refuses base no_base_to_record and otherwise gains no base and no marker. merge.at puts back a merge taken out: the marker of those sides, head and that at — one the board put on the draft since its last publication — stands again as it stood, its at the landing's; any other at is refused marker_not_restorable, nothing written. A FORK whose source is not head is refused fork_base_moved (fork afresh from the head and land there); a published doc published_target. Each origin must be a document you may read. Never held (an unholdable write): under a stopped node or halted writes it is refused at once. Read the record back with doc_metadata(draft): base, base_copied and merge. Response: ack with at, and head_moved where the head moved.

Create an open link homed in home. Each of from_ (the wire's from — renamed in this schema only, mapped back by the adapter), to, and ty takes one of three forms per slot: a V-spec array, resolved against current arrangements (the recorded endset is the permanent I-spans); {"addrs": [addresses]}, address-denoting — the recorded endset is the names verbatim, one unit subtree span per address, with no resolution and no occupancy requirement; or {"spans": [{"start": address, "width": n}]}, content I-spans recorded verbatim (retrieve_i's shape; each start a content-subspace element position, each width at least 1), with no source and nothing of the named document read — the address form widened to a run. Contents at the addresses are never examined; matching is by address, and names nest by tumbler prefix. Any T4-valid address may be named — a link, a document, or a ghost position nothing will ever occupy. The type slot must be nonempty as given (an empty addrs or spans list, like a V-spec set resolving to nothing, rejects empty_type_resolution); from_ and to may be empty in any form. The optional replaces names the record whose state this link replaces: present, one transaction deposits the link and, at the next address of home's link subspace, a second link typed replaces (1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.12) from the first to the address named; absent is the empty state. At the grants class it is how a re-share names the revocation it follows — a grant is honored only where the state it names is its key's current one, so a replayed share grants nothing. A make_link whose own ty is the replaces type is refused credential_refused:replaces_not_standalone: the member is that type's one writer. A make_link whose own ty is the correspondence type (1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.102.1, the publish shot's own record class under counterpart) is refused credential_refused:correspondence_not_standalone: the shot is that type's one writer, and nothing deposits one by itself; the parent counterpart (1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.102) is an ordinary type. Response: ack_addr with the link's address (the first link's, when replaces is present).

The line read: doc's line numbers, and no text. It answers the line each of positions lies on, the position each of lines starts at, and doc's line count — the count always; ask either list alone, or neither. A line break is the single byte 0x0A at its own position (one byte of per-byte text): \r and U+2028 are none, and an atom holds none, whatever its bytes. Line 1 starts at position 1 and line N one position past line break N-1; text after the last line break is a line, a document ending in a line break has no empty last line, and an empty document has no line. A position is answered from 1 to one past the end (where an insert at the end would land). Response: line_numbers — {"positions": [{"line", "masked"}], "lines": [{"start": {"subspace", "ordinal"}, "masked"} or null], "count": {"n", "masked"}}, one item per entry in request order, each number a decimal string; null stands in the place of a line that names none (line 0, or any line past the count). masked is true where a run you may not read lies at or before what the number numbers (anywhere in the document, for the count): its line breaks are counted nowhere, so a line number is your own view — hand another reader a position with its as_of, or a permanent address, never a line number. It numbers the document as it stands at the answer's as_of, the state a burst placed by these numbers is typed against (THE TYPED STATE). Refusals, as data: doc_not_registered; withheld, a document you may not read; not_content_subspace for a position outside the content subspace and range_not_present for one at ordinal 0 or more than one past the end, each naming the position by site.index, the first faulty one speaking; too_many_items for a document of more runs than one walk may pass.

The shell's held call: your held bursts at the board, in resend order — each {held (the ordinal resolve takes), doc, base, frame (the write as composed), cause (why it is held: unreachable, halted, poisoned, durability, behind, moved, head_unreadable (the board's head record cannot be read — it stands damaged, was served garbled, or a claimed board serves none — so the shell cannot sign the write: held on disk and skipped at each probe until the record reads, or dropped), session_died (this adapter's session ended at the burst's dial, or at the shell's read just after the board refused it arrangement_moved — a board restart among the causes — so the write ran nothing: held until a session of yours that may write stands, then sent), a refused run's token — the board's own, a code the shell holds no row for among them, refused at a resend and handed to you at once — or answers_lost: the shell stopped resending: no landing two minutes after the line's first failed send; its refusal names the last answer and the time elapsed), sent (whether the write may have landed: a dial of it was attempted, its answer lost or still to come), time, refusal? (the board's verdict on a refused run, or on a burst held moved as typed against an older state; the shell's own for answers_lost, {kind, name, last, elapsed_ms}; the session's end for session_died, its reason beside it), sendable? (on a moved document's first moved line: true where resolve send would shift it into the text as it now stands, false where it would be held moved again, absent where the shell does not know; a burst sent through these tools carries no anchors, so it never shifts and reads false), hands? (on each moved line of a moved document: whose writes moved it, each once, for the move the document stands on now — each {key, fingerprint?, label?}: own (this key), other (another key, its fingerprint, and its label where the account's records give one), bare (an unsigned write), lost (the board lost whose write it was), the one hand unread (not read yet: the shell reads them again on its own, so list again later), or the one hand unknowable (the board no longer keeps the history that would name them, so they can never be read); absent where the rows name none), again? (beside hands, true: the board refused the line again with no change since your resolve send, and hands are the changes it named before), unwritable? (the shell could not write this line to disk, and says why: the line stands in memory alone until the shell writes it, trying again on its own, and is lost if the process ends first; absent once it is on disk), unwritable_class? (beside unwritable, always with it: full, read_only or other)}. Empty once every held burst has landed or been dropped. Response: a JSON array.

The shell's resolve call: your act on a held burst — "drop" marks the line (and the lines behind it on its document) dropped, given up for good, in any state: a refused run, a moved document, a line that the shell handed back to you (answers_lost), or one still holding, whatever its cause — head_unreadable among them (the board's head record cannot be read, so the shell cannot sign the write, and the line would otherwise wait for a repair that may never come) — save a line with sent true, holding or handed back as answers_lost, which may have landed after all: its drop reads first, and where its write landed keeps the line, nothing dropped and the lines behind it sent in order, answering {"kept": true}; where the read cannot tell whether it landed, nothing is dropped and the drop is refused landing_unread {held, why}, why unanswered (the board gave the read no answer), unread (it answered no page), undecided (a row could be the line's landing and is not confirmed), or stopped, poisoned or halted (a hold standing at the board, no read made): drop it again once the board answers and takes writes, or, a line handed back, send it, and the board judges the send by its typed state; a line whose every dial the shell knows never left this device is dropped with no read, whatever its sent says. A drop that takes lines which may already be on the board — sent true, with no read of the drop's own ruling that out: a refused run's or a moved document's line, or a line behind the one its read found unlanded — answers their ordinals in may_have_landed: they are dropped all the same, and their words may stand, so read the document before writing them again. "send" hands a refused run, a moved document or a line handed back to the resend: a line that may have landed (sent true) is read first and kept where it landed, and otherwise sent again, its two-minute clock started afresh; on a moved document, it first records that the changes which moved it have been seen: a document moved again names only the changes since; one refused again with no change since names again the changes it named before. "send" on a line still holding is not_resolvable: the shell sends it itself as the board takes it. Either act on a line the shell is sending at that moment is not_resolvable until that send ends. An ordinal that stands no longer is no_such_held. Response: {}, {"kept": true} where a drop kept the line, or {"may_have_landed": [<ordinal>, …]} where a drop took lines that may already be on the board.

The shell's publication.open call, a publication's first step (PUBLISHING): the shell reads your draft, the runs of it you select and every link on their words, and holds a PANEL for this session — nothing written — which publication_count, publication_confirm and publication_cancel act on. Give doc, the published document of yours whose version chain the member joins, or mint, the account a new published document is minted under with the member its first — never both. Give also, other private drafts of yours of the same document whose words this publication re-mints as the document's own beside the draft's, each keeping a record of where its words went. The wire's publish may also carry supersede, the daughters a merged version takes in, each a supersession claim in the same write: this open composes it from the draft's merge marker (doc_metadata's merge, set where a merge was landed in the draft) — the published daughters it names, only where the marker's head is the document's newest version by one direct read, never at a draft-side or a fork's merge — and answers it as count.supersede. The shell reads the draft's base itself, never from you — the base the board records for a draft staged with stage, moved to the member each publication of it makes, which doc_metadata(draft) answers as base (PUBLISHING) — and refuses a draft the board records none for, base_unrecorded {draft, doc, reason}, reason no_record (a draft you minted and never staged), other_chain (a base in another document's chain) or free_standing (an alternative of a draft with no base). It types that base's standing against the document's newest version, told before you act: at_head (the member becomes the newest version), behind (a newer version stands, and the member lands beside it as the base's daughter: told, never refused), first (the document has no version yet) or superseded_first (the draft was begun from the document itself and version 1 has since been published: told, never refused — the member lands beside version 1 as its daughter). Response: the panel {rows, formatting, read_with, count, price, windows, parts, inherited, merge_records, edition_links, p3_stands, standing?, head?, left_behind, hold?}, head at behind alone, the newest version's address. rows: the sets of links on the selected words — own, notes, private, then public — each {home, kind, label, links, types, line, read_through, unchanged, fold, changed_types, unchanged_types}; a private row is OFF, its links left out, until switches.on names it. types: the row's links folded by type, each fold {ty, n, far} — ty the type's address, n how many of those links carry it, far each document they point into off the selected words, in address order. unchanged: the row's links unchanged since the draft's base — made before that version and lying only on words it held, none on words this version publishes as new — by address; fold: {unchanged, changed}, the row's links counted so; a private row whose every link is unchanged needs no new decision, its links having stayed private when that version was published, and where the base is the document itself, or there is none (mint), no link is unchanged. changed_types and unchanged_types: that fold by type over the row's changed links alone and over its unchanged links alone — what a row's new links are and reach is changed_types, types also counting the links that need no new decision; a document links on both sides point into stands in both. edition_links: how many of the document's own links lie on the words this publication adds as new: each stays on the draft's earlier words, where a reader who cannot read the draft meets it as withheld, nothing written for it and no answer here changing it. p3_stands: whether the panel holds anything to decide or to say before the write — a private row with a changed link, the formatting line's marks or removals, a re-offered original (a link of yours accepted before, offered again where this version brings in words its copy does not reach, and at no later version), a public row's link on words this version publishes as new, or edition_links above zero. formatting: {marks, cut, removals}, the formatting line. read_with: per published document of yours, whether the edition is read with it now. count: {l, n, r, e, claim, read_with, supersede} with every private row OFF (publication_count says each). price: {lists, body, values, reads, bytes, over}, the request against its caps, over each term past its cap — a non-empty over is refused over_cap at confirm. windows: the runs whose words another unpublished draft of yours holds — a draft named in also excluded, its words published as the document's own — each {run, origin, owner, i_start, width, parts}, cut into parts where a record names some of its words as already published: each part {part, from, ordinal, admits, record?, to?} takes its own answer, keyed "run.part" (publication_count, publication_confirm) — at a part a record names, to the published words it names, counterpart (window them from the version that published them) or drop, a placeholder over words anyone can read there being no answer; at a part none names, publish_first, drop or keep_private — none chosen for you, and a window awaiting its answer counts toward nothing: no row, mark or count is decided on its words until it is answered, publication_count re-keying the panel at each answer. parts: what each part's answer brings, each {run, part, marks, links, kept_marks} — taken by its counterpart, marks the formatting marks on the published words that go out with them and links your private links on them offered next; kept private, kept_marks your formatting marks on its words that stay in your draft until a version shows them; zeros where the part is left out or awaits its answer. inherited: per draft named in also, in that order, {draft, passages}: how many passages of the selection were first written in it, the words that publish as the document's own while that draft keeps a record of where they went. merge_records: per draft whose runs of the selection hold any, {draft, n}: the merge records this publication leaves out — no publication publishes a merge record, so a merge journal's records stay private and stay in its arrangement; a selection of merge records alone is refused only_merge_records {draft}, nothing sent. standing: at_head, behind, first or superseded_first, as above; absent with mint. left_behind: the drafts of yours this publication leaves behind, by address: every draft named in also, then, where the member becomes the newest version (at_head or first), every other draft of yours on the same base; empty with mint. hold: {since}, where a panel of this draft stood behind another and comes back as it stood — a held panel, not a held burst. One panel stands at a time: an open on another draft holds the standing one behind it; an open on a held panel's draft with no selection, or the same one, brings it back where every other member you pass is the panel's — doc or mint, claim, also, notes, readable_drafts, published, one you leave out read as the panel's — and another selection opens it afresh. A member you pass that differs from the panel's, held or standing, is refused other_panel {draft, doc?, mint?} (isError), naming the panel's own doc or mint, nothing read and every panel as it stood: open it with that doc or mint alone, then publication_cancel it for a fresh panel. Without readable_drafts or published, or where the standing is at_head or first, the open waits on the board's index.

The shell's publication.count call, the call per answer: {count, price, rows, formatting, windows, parts, edition_links, p3_stands}, the standing panel re-keyed by the answers sent here at the windows' parts — the rows and their links with each row's unchanged, fold, changed_types and unchanged_types, the formatting line, the windows, what each part's answer brings, the document's own links on the words this publication adds as new (edition_links, as publication_open answers it), whether the panel holds anything to decide (p3_stands, as publication_open answers it) — and its count and price as the switches and answers would leave them, worked off what the open read with nothing sent to the board (PUBLISHING). count {l, n, r, e, claim, read_with, supersede}: l the switched-on rows' links plus the read_with entries the switches need, n the formatting line's marks that re-make nothing, r the retractions no re-make covers, e the re-makes, supersede the supersession claim the one write carries — the published daughters the draft's merge marker names, composed at the open and only where the marker's head is the document's newest version, empty at an unmarked draft, at a marked draft behind the head and at a draft-side merge — claim whether the write carries the edition claim, read_with each switched-on row's destination other than the member, once, where the edition is not read with it yet. price: as publication_open answers it, re-run over the rows as switched. The panel keeps these switches and answers, and shows them where it comes back from behind another; publication_confirm reads none of them — send it its own. No panel standing answers no_panel; a key no window part holds, or an answer the part does not admit, is refused malformed_args naming answers, then a home no private row holds as those answers leave the rows, or a set that is no published document of yours, naming the member.

The shell's publication.confirm call: publishes the standing panel's selection in ONE write the shell composes off the panel and the switches and answers sent here, signs with your key and sends (PUBLISHING). It reads the draft and its base again first, then answers one outcome, as data. {outcome: "acknowledged", member, edition, claim, supersede, at, via}: member the member published (the new published document's first at the mint form, edition then that document, else null), claim whether the edition claim rode in the write, at the commit's position, via how the shell knew it landed (answer, twin, records, walk or edition_claim); supersede the daughters the write claimed superseded, what rode of the panel's count.supersede (a daughter an active claim of yours already named is dropped before the body is signed, as the board skips it) — each marked superseded by the member in the same commit, in_claims at the daughter answering it; the panel is gone. {outcome: "restated", left, superseded, came, removals_undone, removals_came, selection, parts?, left_out?, race?, base?, standing?, head?, marker?}: the draft moved since the panel — links left, superseded or came, held removals undone or come, selected runs placed otherwise, parts window parts a record names now or no longer, each {run, part, record} (its origin published meanwhile: its answer is asked again unless it left the words out) — or its base did, base then the base as read, member or extent differing from the panel's (the draft published again, or a merge landed in it since the panel while it stood on another base: the panel stands re-composed on it, the claim taken again from the merge marker as it stands, so the next confirm sends against that base; a panel of the whole draft re-takes what the draft now arranges, selection then empty, a selection you passed held as it stands over what is left of it), or its merge marker did, marker then the marker as read, {sides, head, head_copied, at}, or null where the draft now carries none (a merge landed in, withdrawn from or undone out of the draft since the panel, none of which need move its base: the panel stands re-composed on it, the claim taken again from it, so no version goes out under a claim the draft no longer carries; a panel of the whole draft re-takes what the draft now arranges, selection then empty), or its base's standing did, standing then the new one, head beside it at behind the newest version's address (behind where another version was published while the panel stood, the head named anew where the draft was behind already; superseded_first where version 1 was, for a draft begun from the document itself — it lands beside version 1 as its daughter), or the board refused an entry by its lineage, left_out [{entry, original, cause}] — cause superseded (the words already carry its copy) or retracted (its original is retracted), race where a change of yours since the reads explains it, else this client offered it again by mistake — the original left out of the panel from then on; nothing was sent: the panel stands re-stated; read it with publication_open on the same draft and confirm again. {outcome: "refused", arm, …}: nothing published, the arm's data beside it — the shell's own before anything is sent, over_cap {over} and inert {inert}: unchanged (the member would change nothing), {unanswered: [{run, part, named}, …]} (a window part left without an answer it admits — named where a record names its words, which take counterpart or drop) or {publish_first: [{run, part}, …]} (a window part answered publish_first: publish its origin first); or the write's: twin, kept_place_moved {index, draft, race} (every draft the panel named — the draft, and each of also — is re-windowed onto the published words in the one write, each at the places the shell read off its own image; draft names the one that no longer holds the entry's words there, moved since the panel, and race whose write moved them: open the panel again and confirm, that draft then left as it stands at the run, healed at its own next publication), unowned_draft, not_owner, claim_refused, window_withheld, needs_signed_session, no_such_document, older_board, head_unreadable, session_ended, budget_race, may_already_stand, base_superseded {first} (the board refused a publish naming no base while the document holds its first version, first — a shape this call never sends at the document form), own_fault {fault} (the shell's own composition at fault, fault.kind among them stray_place {index, draft}) or other. With no panel standing it answers no_panel (isError), and where the board holds writes poisoned or halted it is refused at once with that cause; where the rendering draft, or a draft also names, holds a line of yours the board has not kept (HELD BURSTS) it is refused held_lines {doc, held} (isError), nothing sent — the shot would re-window that draft under words the board never kept: call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then confirm again; where the re-read finds the draft's base no longer recorded it is refused as publication_open refuses it, base_unrecorded (isError); a base or a standing that moved is the restated outcome, never a refusal; where every selected run has left the draft, so nothing of the selection is arranged, it is refused selection_not_arranged {index} (isError), nothing sent, no empty version made: publication_cancel, then publication_open over what the draft now holds.

The shell's publication.standing call: where a draft of yours stands against its document, read alone before you start publishing — no panel composed, none left standing, one standing untouched and nothing written (PUBLISHING). Give draft, the draft; doc, the published document of yours whose version chain it joins, which you name since a draft's base does not say it; and also, the other private drafts of yours a publication of it would re-mint beside it, as publication_open takes them, each named once and never the draft itself. Response: {base, standing, head?, left_behind}. base: the base the board records for the draft, as doc_metadata(draft) answers it, the version its next publication lands after, or doc itself while the chain is empty. standing: that base against the document's newest version, told and never refused — at_head (the member would become the newest version), behind (a newer version stands, and the member would land beside it as the base's daughter), first (the document has no version yet) or superseded_first (the draft was begun from the document itself and version 1 has since been published: the member would land beside version 1 as its daughter). head: at behind alone, the newest version's address. left_behind: the drafts a publication of it would leave behind, by address — every draft also names, then, where it would become the newest version (at_head, first), every other draft of yours whose recorded base is this one's. A draft the board records no base for in doc's chain is refused base_unrecorded {draft, doc, reason}, reason no_record (a draft you minted and never staged), other_chain (a base in another document's chain, doc then not the draft's document) or free_standing (an alternative of a draft with no base); no_such_document and unreadable name doc or the draft, as publication_open's reads do. It is a read: another window holding the board's writes does not refuse it.

The shell's merge.compose call: a published document's head merged with ONE side, and the merge LANDED in a draft of yours, by one write (MERGING). Call merge_compose(doc, alternative, into?), merge_compose(doc, draft, into?) or merge_compose(doc, fork, into?). doc: the published document — the document itself; a version of it is refused malformed_args naming doc. A document with no published version has nothing to merge. The side, exactly one: alternative, a daughter of doc's chain, doc.k.m, a version published beside a newer one (anything else is refused malformed_args naming alternative); or draft, a draft of doc's owner's account whose recorded base — doc_metadata(draft).base — is doc or a version of doc: a draft staged from doc or from a version, or from a draft of yours staged that way; or fork, another account's document whose recorded base (doc_metadata(fork).base), else its source (doc_metadata(fork).source), is doc or a version of doc — its stage or version of one (a draft of doc's owner's account given as fork is refused base_unknown with reason fork_of_owner — give it as draft): it lands into a draft of yours — or, for the fork's owner, into the fork itself, refused merge_refused fork_base_moved {fork, source, head} where its source is not the head, nothing written, while a fork its owner staged — one doc_metadata(fork).base names — takes it at any head, its base moving there (doc itself, a version of it or an address within it is refused malformed_args naming fork). Composed by its owner with no into, a fork lands in a fresh draft of theirs staged from the head: its re-base, which doc's owner then merges as a fork whose base is the head. Two sides are refused malformed_args naming the later of alternative, draft and fork, none naming alternative, draft or fork. into: the draft the merge lands in, an unpublished draft of your own account (not_owner {addr} otherwise), never the draft side itself (malformed_args naming into); best a draft staged from the head, so a call made again re-opens it. With none named, a merge record of yours naming a draft this merge already landed in is read first, and the merge goes there; else a fresh draft is staged from the head. The shell reads the head itself: the trunk's newest version, up from the version the side lies under, or from doc's first version for a side begun from doc itself. The write: M, the merged words at their defaults, as into's whole arrangement, typed against the shell's own read of into; into's recorded base moves to the head, and its merge marker names the side and the head. Response: the report {outcome, doc, head, base, side, form, sides, runs, gaps, counts, cap, over_cap, record, as_of, into?, position?, fresh?, head_moved?, record_link?, unrecorded?, member?, claims?, replaced?}: head the version merged onto, base the version both sides descend from, read off the bases the board recorded and never off an address — doc itself where a side was begun from doc before its first version (a draft or a fork staged from doc, or a daughter published beside version 1), composed over doc as it stood before version 1, empty on most documents, where the texts written apart meet in an order gap you settle by editing into, as at any gap — side and form (daughter, draft or fork) the side merged, sides the record's sides, a fork or draft side with arranged, the position its text last changed at when composed, runs M run by run with the side each came from, counts and cap M's run counts against the cap of one write, record the merge record's body, as_of the one position every read was made at. outcome "landed": into the draft, position the write's commit — your next as_of on into — fresh whether this call staged it, head_moved a newer version published since the head was read, else null (the merge stands on the older head: compose again to merge onto it), record_link the merge record's link, or null with unrecorded the refusal where the record could not be written and the landing stands (the next merge_compose records it). outcome "reopened": into already carries this merge, its marker naming the side and the head — NOTHING landed, each gap's state read off into as it stands, position the first landing's: read into before you write to it. A fork changed since its landing is not re-opened (save into the fork itself): it is composed again on the head and LANDED over into, outcome landed, the earlier landing's words and your edits made in into since replaced — replaced names each stretch it replaced, {ordinal, width, origin, i_start}, ordinals in into as of as_of, [] where none; merge_undo puts them back. outcome "merged": a supersession claim of yours already names the daughter — member the version it names, claims the claims standing at the daughter, record_link and record the merge's record, written now where none of yours stood — nothing landed, and merge_land has nothing to publish. gaps, the gap report, each {id, kind, after, before, runs, placed, settled, resolved_by}: id the key resolutions take; kind order, corner, cut, collision or moves, each unsettled and left at a default, or anchor, settled by the rules; after and before the surviving anchors either side, null at an edge; runs each {side, i_start, width}, the sides numbered 0 for the head and 1 for the side; placed the placement as it stands — the sides' order, after, before or omitted; settled and resolved_by who settled it — rule, agent, or null while it stands at its default. A gap is settled by EDITING into: remove a side's runs whole, or reorder them, then compose again, which reads it settled, resolved_by agent; an edit inside a run's words settles nothing. refused arrangement_moved is data, the board's verdict: into changed while the call read it, nothing landed — call again. Refusals, each isError, nothing written: base_unknown {side, reason, source?, hop?} where the side has no version of doc to merge from — reason base_unknown for a draft never staged, one staged from a draft with no recorded base or from another document, or a draft of another account — compose that one as a fork — and for a fork with neither a recorded base nor a source, one the fork op minted, or one whose recorded base, else its source, is neither doc nor a version of it — a version of a draft, a fork taken from another document, or one published as an edition of its own; reason fork_of_owner for a document of doc's owner's account given as fork, whose draft is the draft side — give it as draft; reason bare_source, naming source (doc itself), for a draft of yours or a fork, of any account, begun from doc while doc has no version yet — nothing to merge onto: publish that draft, which lands version 1 — and, on a board that serves no count of doc's words before version 1, for a side begun from doc, naming the hop, the version on the side's line published from doc, where the side's own base or source is not doc; reason hop_unrecorded, naming the hop, a version on the side's line the board records no base for, its base never taken from its address; not_owner {addr}; over_cap {n, cap} where M is in more runs than one write may name; unreadable {doc}; no_such_document {doc}; merge_refused {arm, …}, landing_begun {draft, position} among its arms (below); held_lines {doc, held} where into, or the draft a merge record of yours names, holds lines of yours the board has not kept (HELD BURSTS): call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then call again; and stopped, poisoned or halted where the board's writes are held. A call answered unreachable, a halt saying the landing stands with its record unwritten, or one that met the end of this adapter's session — which the adapter makes again itself, once, under the next session — may have left a draft it staged, or landed in, that no merge record names. With into named, the call made again re-opens into, or lands there, and stages nothing more, a re-open writing the record of a landing no merge record names where into still holds the merge. With none named, where the merge landed in such a draft, the call — the adapter's own once included — is refused merge_refused landing_begun {draft, position}, nothing staged or written: name draft as into, before you write to it, to re-open it with its record; then merge_undo() takes the merge back, or merge_withdraw(draft) takes it out and keeps its words. A draft only staged, the merge never landed in it, is left standing beside the next one staged: changes_since(class: "drafts") from before the call names such a draft by its stage row, and naming it as into lands there.

The shell's merge.land call: the merge the standing composition landed published from the draft it landed in, in ONE signed write through the publication family's one composition and send (PUBLISHING) — under the panel of yours over that draft at doc, standing or held, with the switches and answers you last sent it, or one the shell opens over the whole draft, every private row OFF — the supersession claim on the daughter riding in it where the draft's merge marker names the trunk's head (none at the draft or fork side, whose side is no version of doc), then the merge record (MERGING). Call merge_land(resolutions?, answers?). resolutions: {gap id: choice}, your choice at each gap, recorded in the merge record; it changes NO words — the draft is published as it stands, so settle a gap by editing the draft first. A choice is keep_both (the default kept), omit, {order: [sides]} (each a side among the gap's runs, none twice), {keep_only: side}, {after: anchor} or {before: anchor} (the gap's own after or before anchor); one naming no gap of the composition, or no choice the gap admits, is refused malformed_args naming resolutions, nothing sent. answers: one answer per window part, keyed "run.part", as publication_confirm takes them; the landing answers NO window part for you — at the fork side the fork's own words are such parts, onto the fork, never re-minted as doc's own. Response: {outcome: "landed", member, at, via, claim, supersede, daughter, record, unrecorded?, claims, retries, answers, left_private, defaults}: member the version published, at its commit, supersede the daughters the write claimed superseded, daughter true where the head moved under a shot that claims none — the draft or fork side's — and the member landed as a daughter beside the head, record the merge record's link, or null with unrecorded the refusal where the record could not be written (the next merge_compose of the daughter records it), claims the claims standing at the daughter, answers each window part's answer as given, left_private each private set the landing left out with its count, defaults each gap left at its default. The composition is gone with the landing: merge_undo then answers no_merge, and a published merge is not undone. {outcome: "restated", left, superseded, came, removals_undone, removals_came, selection, parts?, left_out?, race?, base?, standing?, head?, marker?}: the panel of the draft re-stated, nothing sent — call merge_land again. {outcome: "refused", arm, …}: nothing published, the arm's data beside it; the race is arm supersede_refused with detail head_moved and head the trunk's newest version, as the board answered it — nothing sent again, the composition gone: compose again on that head. Refusals, each isError, nothing sent: window_parts_owed {parts, answers, misfits, left_private, defaults} where a window part is unanswered: parts every part to answer, each {run, part, words, after, ordinal, origin, owner, span, record, counterpart, version, sides, admits, answer, named_since} — call merge_land again with answers keyed "run.part", each one its part admits; no_merge {session} where no composition stands — none composed, published, or gone with this adapter's session, a board restart among the causes — and no_merge {draft} where the draft no longer carries this merge, another landing in it since or a withdrawal: compose again; other_panel {draft, doc?, mint?} where a panel of yours over the draft mints an edition or publishes into another document: publication_cancel it — a held one first opened again in its own form, publication_open with the draft and the doc or mint the refusal names and nothing else — then merge_land again; held_lines {doc, held} where the draft, or the draft side, holds lines of yours the board has not kept (HELD BURSTS): call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then call again; base_unrecorded where the draft was published as a document of its own; and publication_confirm's own. A merge_land answered session_died or unreachable, or no_merge after a session's end, may still have published: at a daughter, merge_compose it again, and merged names the member; at the draft or fork side, doc_metadata(into) — into the draft the compose landed in — names the version published as its base.

The shell's merge.undo call, in two forms (MERGING). merge_undo(): the standing composition's landing taken back out of its draft in ONE write — the arrangement the draft held before the landing, its words mapped through your publications' correspondence records where one made them public since, the base it recorded then, and the merge marker it carried then put back as it stood, or none. It is typed against the landing's position, or that of the write that last put the landing's marker back — never your own last write, since you have no editor's stack that takes your later changes back first — so it lands only where nothing but a take-back of this merge and its undo changed the draft's arrangement since. Past any change — your own edits included — it is refused arrangement_moved — data, the board's verdict, site.as_of the landing's position and site.current the change — NOTHING changed, and the undo can no longer land, since taking the changes back changes the draft again: edit the draft as it stands. Keep the merged words and take the merge out with merge_withdraw(draft); or put back a state before the landing with restore_text(draft, at, as_of) (THE TYPED STATE), which leaves the merge marker and the recorded base the landing set standing, then merge_withdraw(draft) to clear the marker. merge_undo(draft, withdrawal): a merge merge_withdraw took out put back as it stood — the draft's words as they stand, mapped the same way, its recorded base unmoved, and the marker the withdrawal cleared, its sides, its head and the landing's at — withdrawal the position merge_withdraw answered. It is typed against the withdrawal's position the same way, so a change since refuses it arrangement_moved; the composition the withdrawal set aside in this session stands again, so the next merge_undo() takes the landing back. One of draft and withdrawal alone is refused malformed_args naming the other. Response: {draft, position, record, restored, marker?}: position the write's commit, your next as_of on draft; record the replacing merge record's link, or null where none stood; restored the base restored, {base, extent}, or null — always null at the withdrawal's undo; marker, the landing's undo alone, the draft's merge marker as the undo left it, {sides, head, head_copied, at}, or null. Where marker is an earlier landing's whose composition a later landing in the draft set aside in this session, that composition stands again, and the next merge_undo() takes that landing back. Refusals, each isError, nothing sent: no_merge {session} where no composition stands — none composed, published by merge_land, taken back already, or gone with this adapter's session, a board restart among the causes; no_merge {draft} where the draft no longer carries the merge, and no_merge {draft, withdrawal} where the position names no withdrawal of the draft; nothing_to_undo {draft, why}, why inherited (the marker came with the draft's stage: no landing in it), taken_back, published, with version (the draft was published since: the way back is to publish the older text again) or remarked (the draft carries a merge again); merge_refused {arm: "history_reclaimed", at, floor} where the board keeps the state before the landing no longer; over_cap {n, cap}; not_owner {addr}; held_lines {doc, held} where the draft holds lines of yours the board has not kept (HELD BURSTS): call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then call again. A withdrawal's undo whose write landed before a session's end has taken effect: called again, it answers nothing_to_undo, why remarked.

The shell's merge.withdraw call: takes the merge out of a draft of yours and KEEPS its words, in ONE write (MERGING) — the draft's current runs set as its whole arrangement with its recorded base re-sent unmoved and no merge, so its merge marker is cleared and a publication of it claims no daughter superseded. Call merge_withdraw(draft): any draft of yours that carries a merge marker, in any session — one another device or skep merge landed in among them — typed against the shell's own read of the draft. The standing composition on that draft is set aside, for the withdrawal's undo to stand it again. Response: {draft, position, record}: position the write's commit — your next as_of on draft — and the withdrawal's handle: merge_undo(draft, withdrawal: position) puts the merge back as it stood while nothing changed the draft's arrangement since; record the replacing merge record's link, or null where no record of the landing stood. refused arrangement_moved is data, the board's verdict: the draft changed while the shell read it, nothing changed — call again, which reads it as it stands. Refusals, each isError, nothing sent: no_merge {draft} where the draft carries no merge marker; not_owner {addr} where it is another account's, and not_owner {addr, published: true} for a published document; unreadable {doc}; no_such_document {doc}; held_lines {doc, held} where the draft holds lines of yours the board has not kept (HELD BURSTS): call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then call again. A withdrawal whose write landed before a session's end has taken effect: called again, it answers no_merge {draft} — read doc_metadata(draft).merge before you compose again.

The shell's changes call as a pull: what changed on the board since the log position since, at your reader class — {entries, next, head}. Each entry is a /changes row with its position and class (published, or drafts for a draft you may read): {position, at, op, docs, class, session? (on a drafts entry, the shell session it was read under, never its writer), by? (on a drafts entry, the shell session that wrote it, where one of this adapter's did: the entry's own session, or an earlier one of this adapter's from before a board restart; absent for a write of another device's, another program's or another principal's), burst? (on a drafts entry, the id a page sent on the burst the entry carries; your bursts carry none), key? (on an unsigned entry, the board's testimony: the fingerprint of the key whose session committed it, "bare" or "system"), time?, attest? (on a signed entry, its signature), link?, new_prefix?, new_id?, placed?, base_extent?, base?, merge? (on a set_arrangement entry: base the base it recorded, or null; merge {sides, head} where it landed a merge, with at where it put a taken-out merge back, else null — an undo or a withdrawal names a base and no merge, a plain re-arrangement neither)}, oldest first. next is the position to ask from next time — keep it; head the board's latest position. Bounded by limit and the board's page budget; a since below the board's memory is refused history_reclaimed naming the floor. Start from session_info's health.log_position, or from 0. With class "drafts" the page is the drafts rows alone — the entries naming a draft you may read, nothing published — read from since under your session; any other class is refused malformed_args naming class. With under, an address — a draft, a document or an account — every read is narrowed to the rows naming a document at or under it: one draft's history, a row per change with its hand and its time; a draft you may not read answers no row. A narrowed next is a position of the narrowed feed, past rows it never read: keep one next per under you read, and never pass a narrowed next as the since of a page read without it.

The bytes of the picture whose reference cell sits at the I-address i (doc.0.1.ordinal), fetched whole from the board under your session and checked by the board against the cell's hash and size before its first byte. The result is one content block: an image block (mimeType image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp) where the bytes' magic names one — the type is sniffed off the bytes by this adapter and never attested by the board, which declares none — else an embedded resource blob of application/octet-stream at the fetch's own URI. A file past this adapter's cap of 8 MiB (8388608 bytes) is refused naming the cap — no byte of it read where the board declares its length, as skepd always does — and a stream cut short, or still unfinished at ten and a half minutes (an honest board's own bound), is said so: each isError, its text a plain sentence; a file you may not read is withheld; a cell that is none is not_a_cell. The client-side recovery order is not run: the bytes are what the board served.

Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: replace this exact text with that, in a draft — the text edit, one call with no position to count. doc is a draft you own; old is text the draft holds now, which must stand EXACTLY ONCE in it (quote enough of the text around your change to make it so); new is the text to stand in its place, and an empty new removes old. The adapter reads the draft's content as text, finds old, leaves standing what old and new share at their start and their end, and replaces ONLY THE BYTES THAT DIFFER, through insert and delete: every other byte of the draft — the unchanged part of the very line you edit among them — keeps its identity, so a link, a transclusion or a comparison on it still holds, where retyping a line, or setting the whole text afresh, mints it anew and leaves every link on the old words behind. Use it for every change you can say as old text and new text; move whole lines with move_lines, which retypes nothing. insert, delete, copy, reinstate, rearrange and set_arrangement stay yours for the rest: the first text of an empty draft, words placed by identity, a move that is not whole lines, an atom. Positions are bytes: text is one value a byte (ENCODINGS), and an atom, or any other value that is no per-byte text, is no text, so old never matches across one. A published document is never edited in place: it is refused published, and changes by publishing a draft staged from it (PUBLISHING). It reads the draft itself and types its writes against that read: you pass no as_of. Response, one JSON object by outcome. {outcome: "replaced", doc, ordinal, removed, inserted, addr?, at?}: the edit landed — ordinal the content position (1-based, a byte each) of the first byte changed, removed and inserted the bytes taken out and put in there, addr the first I-address of the new bytes (absent where none was inserted), at the commit the edit was whole at, which is the as_of your next burst on doc is typed against. {outcome: "unchanged", doc, ordinal, as_of}: old and new are the same text, found once at ordinal; nothing written. {outcome: "refused", cause, doc, …}: NOTHING of this edit stands and no line of it is held — cause not_found (count 0) or not_unique (count: in how many places old stands; quote more of the text), each with the as_of the draft was read at; crosses_atom (ordinal, kind: old matches only across a value that is no text); published (published: the document); too_large (what: new, a changed text past one insert's cap of 262144 bytes, or draft, a draft past 8388608 content positions — bytes or positions, and cap); unknown_item (kind: a value whose positions this adapter cannot count); or the board's own refusal of the write, its code as cause and its verdict verbatim under refusal — arrangement_moved where the draft changed after this call read it, or between two parts of a long draft's read, then with the read's as_of and no verdict (call again: the edit is made against the text as it then stands), not_owner for a draft that is not yours. The same object with isError true is a write the shell could not get to the board — cause unreachable, stopped, halted, poisoned, durability, head_unreadable, session_died, or behind (a line of an earlier burst of yours is held at this board: held(), resolve it, then call again) — or cause unread (op: a read the board answered in a form this adapter does not read): nothing standing either way. A change that both removes and inserts is TWO commits, no operation doing both in one: the new text is inserted directly after the old, then the old is removed; where the removal does not land — another writer's change between the two — the insert is taken back within the call, found by its identity wherever it stands, and the answer is the refusal, nothing standing. Two answers, each isError, say that something of the edit stands or may. {outcome: "partial", doc, new_text: {ordinal, width, addr?, at?}, old_text: {ordinal, width}, cause, refusal?, op?}: the new text STANDS directly after the old text, which was NOT removed, and the take-back did not land, no line of this edit held — new_text and old_text the two spans as they stood at the insert's commit (at), and op, where cause is unread, the write whose answer this adapter could not read: read the draft (image finds addr wherever it has moved to), then delete one of the two, old_text to finish the edit or new_text to undo it, typed at your read's as_of, or call replace_text with old the two together. {outcome: "held", doc, held, cause, write, new_text?, old_text?}: the shell could not tell whether this edit's write (write: insert, delete or undo) landed, the board not answering, so its line stays held (HELD BURSTS): once the board answers, resolve(held, "drop") — kept means the write landed, {} that it did not — then read the draft; with new_text and old_text beside it the edit is of two writes and may stand in part: a held insert may have placed new_text, a held delete may have removed old_text, and a held undo — the take-back of new_text, sent because the removal of old_text did not land — may have removed new_text, old_text standing: kept then means nothing of this edit stands, {} that both texts do. A call that ends with no answer at all — the adapter stopped between the two commits — may have left those two spans too: read the draft before you edit it again. A document that is none, or that you may not read, answers the board's refusal of the read, as data (REJECTIONS ARE DATA).

Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: several edits of a draft's text in ONE call, all landing or none, answered with the lines they changed. Call edit_text(doc, edits: [{old, new}, …]): doc a draft you own; each old must stand EXACTLY ONCE in the draft as the pairs before it leave it (pairs apply in order), new stands in its place, an empty new removing old; at most 4096 pairs. ALL OR NOTHING: every pair is checked against one read before anything is written — a pair whose old is not found once refuses the call, naming it (pair) — and a write past the first that does not land sets the draft back exactly as it stood. Each pair is made as its smallest changes, so text between two changes keeps its identity and its links. ROWS: a landed call's result is the answer object on line 1, then one row a line, numbered in the draft as the call left it, as line_numbers counts lines; <TAB> is a tab. "+N<TAB>line": a line holding a byte the call put in, or where a removal inside a line left it; " N<TAB>line" (a space, then N): one of the 2 unchanged lines either side; "-<TAB>(N bytes removed here)": whole lines went here, between the lines that now meet (", at the text's end" before the ")" at the end); "--" parts rows whose lines do not touch; a run of more than 16 + rows shows its first 6, "+…<TAB>(N more lines)", its last 3; a line past 2000 characters ends "…[+N chars]"; non-UTF-8 bytes show as {hex:…}, a value that is no text as {…}; past 40000 bytes the rows end "(N more changed lines not shown)". masked: true: a withheld run stands at or before a shown line, so the numbers are your view. pairs' ordinals are each in the draft as the changes before it left it. partial and held are isError: part of the call stands, or may — read the draft before you edit it again; stands names each change at its own commit, its new bytes found by addr. Response: one JSON object by outcome, the rows after it where the call landed. {outcome: "edited", doc, pairs: [[change, …], …], at?, masked?}: every change landed — pairs lists each pair's changes in its order, none for a pair whose old and new are the same text, a change {ordinal, removed, inserted, addr?, at?}: ordinal the content position (1-based, a byte each) of its first byte in the draft as the changes before it left it, removed and inserted the bytes taken out and put in there, each a decimal string, addr the first I-address of its new bytes (absent where none was inserted), at the commit it was whole at; the object's at is the commit the call was whole at, the as_of your next burst on doc is typed against, absent where the last write's answer named none. {outcome: "unchanged", doc, as_of}: every old stands once and each new is the same text, in the draft as read at as_of; nothing written. {outcome: "refused", cause, doc, …}: NOTHING of the call stands and no line of it is held — cause not_found (count 0) or not_unique (count: in how many places old stands; quote more of the text), each with the as_of the draft was read at, crosses_atom (ordinal, kind: old matches only across a value that is no text), each with pair, the index in edits of the pair refused, its old sought in the text as the pairs before it leave it; published (published: the document); too_large (what: new, a change's new text past one insert's cap of 262144 bytes, with bytes, pair and change; draft, a draft past 8388608 content positions, with positions; or runs, a draft in more runs than one write sets back, with runs where the board's image named them — and cap); unknown_item (kind: a value whose positions this adapter cannot count); arrangement_moved where the draft changed after this call read it (call again: the edits are made against the text as it then stands); or the board's own refusal of a write, its code as cause and its verdict verbatim under refusal, with pair and change, the change whose write it refused — not_owner for a draft that is not yours. The same object with isError true is a write the shell could not get to the board — cause unreachable, stopped, halted, poisoned, durability, head_unreadable, session_died, or behind (a line of an earlier burst of yours is held at this board: held(), resolve it, then call again) — or cause unread (op: a read the board answered in a form this adapter does not read): nothing standing either way. Two answers, each isError, name what stands. {outcome: "partial", doc, cause, refusal?, op?, pair, change, stands, take_back?: {cause, refusal}, may_stand?}: the call stopped at the change change of the pair pair and the draft was NOT set back — another writer's change landed between two of the call's writes (cause arrangement_moved, its verdict under refusal: nothing is taken back over another's change), a write landed with no commit this adapter read (cause unread or answer_lost, op the write: nothing written after it), or the one write that sets the draft back did not land (take_back: what refused it, never sent again; may_stand where its answer was lost, so each change of stands may stand or not). {outcome: "held", doc, held, cause, write, pair, change, stands}: the shell could not tell whether a write of the call's landed, the board not answering, so its line stays held (HELD BURSTS) and nothing was written after it or taken back (write: insert, delete or undo — undo the removal by identity of a change's new text): once the board answers, resolve(held, "drop") — kept means the write landed, {} that it did not — then read the draft. stands: [{pair, change, ordinal, removed, inserted, addr?, at?} or {pair, change, new_text: {ordinal, width, addr?, at?}, old_text: {ordinal, width}}] — each change that stands, in the order written: whole, at its own commit, its ordinal in the draft as the changes before it left it, so a later change may have moved it (image finds addr wherever it stands); or in part, the last, its new text standing directly after its old text, which was not removed, the two spans as its insert left them — beside a held insert new_text may be placed, beside a held delete old_text may be removed, beside a held undo new_text may be removed while old_text stands. A call that ends with no answer at all may have left any of that standing: read the draft before you edit it again. replace_text still edits one pair, and answers as help("replace_text") says. A document that is none, or that you may not read, answers the board's refusal of the read, as data (REJECTIONS ARE DATA).

Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: whole lines of a draft moved to another place in it, in ONE call, by identity, answered with the lines where they now stand. Call move_lines(doc, first, last?, before?): doc a draft you own; the lines first to last, both included (last absent: the one line first), move to stand before the line before — absent, or one past the last line, the end of the text; each a whole number from 1, and before never inside the block (past first, and at or before last). Lines are numbered as line_numbers counts them: a line break is the byte 0x0A, an atom or any other value that is no text holds none, text after the last line break is a line, and a text ending in a line break has no empty last line. Take the numbers from a read or an answer made after your last change: a change moves every line after it. The adapter reads the draft itself, finds where the lines start, and moves them by ONE rearrange typed against that read: you count no position and pass no as_of. NO BYTE IS MINTED: every byte moved keeps its identity, so a link, a transclusion or a comparison on it still holds and the change reads as a move — where removing the lines and typing them again (edit_text, or two replace_text calls) mints them anew and leaves every link on them behind. The lines move exactly as given: to carry a blank line with a block, include it. A value that is no text moves with its line. rearrange itself stays yours for a move that is not whole lines. A published document is never edited in place: it is refused published (PUBLISHING). ROWS: a landed call's result is the answer object on line 1, then one row a line, numbered in the draft as the call left it, as line_numbers counts lines; <TAB> is a tab. "+N<TAB>line": a moved line, where it now stands; " N<TAB>line" (a space, then N): one of the 2 unchanged lines either side; "-<TAB>(lines A–B moved to C–D)", or "-<TAB>(line A moved to C)" for one line: where the lines left, A and B their numbers before the call, C and D now; "--" parts rows whose lines do not touch; a long run of + rows, a long line, non-UTF-8 bytes, a value that is no text and the rows' byte bound are shown as help("edit_text") says. masked: true: a withheld run stands at or before a shown line, so the numbers are your view. Response: one JSON object by outcome, the rows after it where the call landed. {outcome: "moved", doc, first, last, to_first, to_last, cuts, at?, masked?}: the lines moved — first and last the lines as you named them, to_first and to_last the lines they now stand at; cuts the three or four content positions the rearrange was sent about, each a decimal string; at its commit, the as_of your next burst on doc is typed against, absent where the write's answer was lost and the shell's read found it landed. Where the text ends in no line break and its last line moves up, or lines move down to its end, four cuts keep a line break between the two, so every line stays whole and the text still ends in none. One case differs: where such a move crosses exactly one empty line, or moves one empty line to the end, that line's break now ends the text, which holds one line fewer — the row where the lines left then follows the last line, and an empty line moved to the end is no line: to_first and to_last are one past the last line and no + row is shown. {outcome: "unchanged", doc, as_of}: the lines stand before that line already (before is first, or one past last), in the draft as read at as_of; nothing written. {outcome: "refused", cause, doc, …}: NOTHING moved and no line of the call is held — cause no_such_line (what: first, last or before, the argument naming a line the draft does not hold; line: the line it names; count: how many lines the draft holds — first and last name a line from 1 to count, before one from 1 to one past it): read the draft, or ask line_numbers, and call again; published (published: the document); too_large (what: draft, a draft past 8388608 content positions, with positions and cap); unknown_item (kind: a value whose positions this adapter cannot count); arrangement_moved where the draft changed after this call read it — between two parts of a long draft's read, then with the read's as_of, or before the rearrange landed, then with the board's verdict verbatim under refusal: nothing was written and your line numbers may be stale, so read the draft again, then call again; or the board's own refusal of the write, its code as cause and its verdict under refusal — not_owner for a draft that is not yours. The same object with isError true is a write the shell could not get to the board — cause unreachable, stopped, halted, poisoned, durability, head_unreadable, session_died, or behind (a line of an earlier burst of yours is held at this board: held(), resolve it, then call again) — or cause unread (op: a read the board answered in a form this adapter does not read): nothing standing either way. {outcome: "held", doc, held, cause, write}, isError: the shell could not tell whether the call's one write (write: rearrange) landed, the board not answering, so its line stays held (HELD BURSTS): once the board answers, resolve(held, "drop") — kept means the lines moved, {} that they stand where they stood — then read the draft. A document that is none, or that you may not read, answers the board's refusal of the read, as data (REJECTIONS ARE DATA).

Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: a mark of a draft — a private document of your account holding the draft's whole content by identity, kept to diff against later — made in ONE call. Call mark_text(doc): doc the draft, a document you may read. The adapter reads the draft's extent, then makes three writes: create_new_document in your account, private; one copy of the draft's whole content into it, which the board clips to what the draft holds at the copy's commit — NO BYTE IS MINTED, the mark holds the draft's very bytes — a draft read empty not copied; and one link typed marks (the commons type 1.1.0.1.0.1.0.3.25), homed in the mark, its from the mark's whole content and its to the draft: the link says what the document is and which draft it marks, so find_links_ftt by that type, to the draft, finds a draft's marks. Use it before work you will review: mark, change the draft, then diff_text(doc, since: the mark). A mark is no staged draft: it records no base and no source, no publication of the draft lists or offers it, and it is kept among your documents as every document is. Response: one JSON object by outcome. {outcome: "marked", doc, mark, link, at}: mark the new document's address, to pass as since; link the marks link's address; at the link's commit. {outcome: "refused", cause, doc, …}: no mark was made and no line of the call is held — the board's refusal of the copy, its code as cause and its verdict under refusal, with mark beside it: the empty document the create left, nothing copied into it and no link written. The same object with isError true is a copy the shell could not get to the board — cause unreachable, stopped, halted, poisoned, durability, head_unreadable, session_died, or behind (a line of an earlier burst of yours is held at this board: held(), resolve it, then call again), mark naming the empty document — or cause unread (op: a read or the create, answered in a form this adapter does not read). {outcome: "held", doc, mark, held, cause, write}, isError: the shell could not tell whether the copy (write: copy) landed, the board not answering, so its line stays held (HELD BURSTS): once the board answers, resolve(held, "drop") — kept means the mark holds the draft's content, {} that it holds nothing — and either way it carries no marks link. {outcome: "partial", doc, mark, at?, cause, refusal?, op?}, isError: the create and the copy landed and the link did not — the board refused it (slot_too_large: the mark holds more runs than a link's end takes), or its answer was lost — so mark STANDS, usable as since, with no marks link; at the copy's commit (the create's for a draft read empty; absent where the copy's own answer was lost); cause the refusal's name with the refusal beside it, or unread with op. partial is isError, and the link is not sent again. A draft that is none, or that you may not read, answers the board's refusal of the read, and an account with no home yet the create's mint_home_first, each as data, nothing written (REJECTIONS ARE DATA); a board stopped, poisoned or halted refuses the call before any read, isError.

Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: what changed in a draft since an earlier state of it, told BY IDENTITY, in ONE call that writes nothing. Call diff_text(doc, since, stat?, hunk?): doc the draft; since a document whose content the draft holds by identity — a mark (mark_text), the version member the draft was staged from, or a document it copied from; stat: true answers the counts alone and reads no text; hunk, a whole number from 1, starts the rows at that hunk. skep knows which bytes of since still stand in the draft: the adapter reads the two documents' images, comparing no text to find what they share, then the draft's text, and — by identity (retrieve_i) — only the spans the draft holds nowhere; since is never read whole. So a block moved by move_lines or rearrange is the same bytes at another place and shows as MOVED, and text deleted and typed again is new bytes that read the same and is said RE-TYPED, where a text diff shows the first as a deletion and an addition and nothing of the second. Of the stretches the two share, the heaviest set that keeps its order stays, and the rest moved. Both texts are mapped first through the correspondence records the publications left, each draft's read in its owner's account, yours or another account's whose draft you hold words of, by the mapping restore_text makes of a past state: words a publication re-minted pair with since, so only real edits show. ROWS: the result is the answer object on line 1, then the hunks, one row a line; <TAB> is a tab. "@@ -a,b +c,d @@" heads a hunk: its first line and its count of lines in since, then in the draft, with the 2 unchanged lines either side of its changes.
