" N<TAB>line" (a space, then N): a line unchanged, N its number in the draft; "-N<TAB>line": a line gone, drawn from since and numbered in it; "+N<TAB>line": a line new; ">N<TAB>line": a line MOVED here, its identity kept; "<<TAB>(lines A–B moved to C–D)", or "<<TAB>(line A moved to C)" for one line: where moved lines left, A and B their numbers in since, C and D in the draft. a run of more than 16 +, - or > rows shows its first 6, a row of its own sign such as "-…<TAB>(N more lines)", its last 3; "\ no line break at the end" follows a last line that has none; a long line, non-UTF-8 bytes and a value that is no text are shown as help("edit_text") says, and a line holding a value that is no text equals no other. The rows stop after the last whole hunk that fits 40000 bytes, next_hunk then naming the hunk to ask next; one hunk past the bound alone ends "(N more changed lines not shown)". Response: one JSON object by outcome, the rows after it. {outcome: "diffed", doc, since, as_of, shared, bytes: {new, gone, moved}, lines?: {added, removed, moved}, notes?, masked?, next_hunk?}: as_of the position the draft was read at; shared the positions of the draft that since holds too; bytes the change by identity — new the positions of the draft since holds nowhere, gone the positions of since that neither stay nor moved, moved the positions of the draft that moved or stand a second time — and lines the lines added, removed and moved here; every count a decimal string. With stat: true, and where the two share nothing and neither is empty (shared "0": since shares nothing with the draft — check that since is its mark), shared and bytes are the whole answer and no rows follow. notes, a list: {kind: "moved", before: [A, B], now: [C, D]}, lines that moved, their first and last in since and in the draft; {kind: "placed_twice", before, now}, lines that stand here by identity and at another place of the draft too; {kind: "retyped", before, now}, lines equal as text whose every byte is new, said for a block of 8 or more characters that are no whitespace; {kind: "moved_within_lines", bytes}, moved bytes no whole line holds. masked: true: a withheld run stands at or before a shown line, so the numbers are your view; a stretch of since you may not read is shown as a value that is no text. {outcome: "unchanged", doc, since, as_of}: nothing changed. {outcome: "refused", cause, doc, …}: nothing is written, ever — cause arrangement_moved (reads: how many times the draft was read and found changed under the call): call again; too_large (what: draft or since, a text past 8388608 content positions, with positions and cap — stat: true reads no text and still answers its counts — or pairs, two documents sharing more stretches than 65536, with pairs and cap); no_such_hunk (hunk, and count: how many hunks the diff holds); unknown_item (kind: a value whose positions this adapter cannot count). The same object with isError true is cause unread (op: a read the board answered in a form this adapter does not read). A document that is none, or that you may not read, or one in more runs than the board images (image_too_large), answers the board's refusal of the read, as data (REJECTIONS ARE DATA).

Adapter apparatus, not a wire operation: the shell's history.restore call — a draft you own put back as it stood at an earlier position, in ONE write, BY IDENTITY. Call restore_text(draft, at, as_of). draft: the draft. at: a position the draft stood at in the state you want — the as_of of a read of it made before the change (retrieve_v, image, line_numbers and doc_metadata each answer one), an earlier edit's at (the state that edit left), or the at of a changes_since(under: draft) row before the change. as_of: your typed state of the draft (THE TYPED STATE) — the as_of of your last read of it or the at of your own last ack on it, whichever is later; never session_info's log_position: the board refuses only a state older than the draft's last change, so a restore typed at the board's head takes back changes you never read. The shell reads the draft's state as of at, and the correspondence records your publications left, then sets that state as the draft's whole arrangement by ONE set_arrangement typed against as_of, naming no base and no merge. NO BYTE IS MINTED: the old words come back as the very bytes they were, and every link on them comes back with them, where retyping the old text (replace_text, edit_text) mints it anew and leaves every link on it behind. It takes back EVERY change made since at, yours and any other hand's. Words of that state published since come back as the published words they became, never the draft's own bytes, which the board refuses already_published; the draft's base and its merge marker stand as they are. Response: {draft, at, position, as_of, marker}. position: the write's commit, the as_of your next write on draft is typed against. as_of: a position the draft stood at before the write. marker: the draft's merge marker as it stands — a restore never takes one out, so a restore to a state before a merge landed leaves it standing — or null. The way back is restore_text(draft, at: as_of, as_of: position): the answer's own as_of, typed at its position, puts back the state the restore replaced. refused arrangement_moved is data (REJECTIONS ARE DATA), the board's verdict, site.as_of your as_of and site.current the change past it: the draft changed past your as_of, and NOTHING changed — read the draft, then call again at that read's as_of. The shell's own refusals are isError, nothing written: merge_refused {arm: "not_past", draft, at, current} where at is at or past current, the draft's position; {arm: "history_reclaimed", at, floor} where the board keeps that state no longer — past states are kept back to the board's oldest kept checkpoint, floor the oldest position it still answers, or null where it names none; {arm: "not_a_position", at, nearest} where at falls inside one commit, nearest the position below it, to call again with; {arm: "history_busy"}, the board's reads of past states all in use: call again in a moment; {arm: "too_fragmented", doc, runs_seen} where that state is in more pieces than the board's image read answers; {arm: "window_withheld", origin} where the state shows words of a document you may not read; held_lines {doc, held} where the draft holds lines of yours the board has not kept (HELD BURSTS): call held(), resolve each line on that doc, then call again; not_owner {addr, published: true} for a published document, never restored in place (PUBLISHING), and not_owner {addr} for a draft of another account's; no_such_document {doc} for a draft that is none or did not exist at at, and unreadable {doc}; over_cap {n, cap} where the state is in more runs than one write may name; no_account; another_window (REJECTIONS ARE DATA); and stopped, poisoned or halted {op: "set_arrangement"} where the board's writes are held (HELD BURSTS), refused before any read — the shell's own, unlike the board's poisoned verdict below. The board's other verdicts are data: write_busy and durability did nothing and are not reissued — call again; poisoned may land when the board restarts, and internal_panic may have committed — read the draft before you call again (REJECTIONS ARE DATA). unreachable (isError) may have landed: call again with the same draft, at and as_of — nothing is written twice. In the same session the board answers with the first write's acknowledgment where it landed, from its memo: position the first write's, as_of yours. After the session has ended, a landed first write is refused arrangement_moved — as is one the memo no longer holds: read the draft. A restore that met the end of this adapter's session ran nothing, and is reissued once under the session that stands, typed at the same as_of.
